Industry News: Ancient rocks from the Moon’s far side rewrite the Solar System’s violent past

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (826 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that ancient rocks collected from the Moon's far side are revealing upcoming details about the violent events that shaped the early Solar System.
  • It has been revealed that latest research suggests that the intense asteroid bombardment experienced by the Moon did not occur primarily during a single, catastrophic period, as scientists previously believed.
  • The Moon offers a rare opportunity to investigate this distant past.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that ancient rocks collected from the Moon's far side are revealing upcoming details about the violent events that shaped the early Solar System. The discoveries are challenging a scientific theory that has stood for decades and could also provide crucial clues about the conditions that influenced Earth's earliest history.

It has been revealed that latest research suggests that the intense asteroid bombardment experienced by the Moon did not occur primarily during a single, catastrophic period, as scientists previously believed. Instead, evidence preserved in lunar rocks indicates that the frequency of these collisions decreased gradually over billions of years.

The Moon offers a rare opportunity to investigate this distant past. While erosion, volcanic activity, and the movement of tectonic plates have destroyed much of Earth's earliest geological record, the lunar surface has retained evidence of ancient asteroid impacts dating back billions of years.

Why the Moon's Far Side Holds Key Clues.

According to recent reports, dr. Fred Jourdan, a research co-author affiliated with Curtin University's School of Earth and Planetary Sciences and John de Laeter Centre, explained that lunar rocks preserve valuable information about the Solar System's earliest history. These natural records allow researchers to investigate events that took place soon after the planets formed.

"The Moon is like a time capsule -- it has preserved a record of events that have been erased from Earth by erosion, plate tectonics and other geological processes," Dr. Jourdan said.

"Samples collected from the Moon's far side are particularly significant because they allow us to compare two very different parts of the Moon for the first time. Until now, almost everything we knew came from the side facing Earth.".

Recent findings suggest that "By analyzing these ancient rocks, we can better understand when major asteroid impacts occurred and how the early Solar System evolved. The far side preserves a cleaner record of those earliest impacts because it was much less affected by later geological events than the side facing Earth.

"These samples are helping us rewrite parts of the Moon's history and suggest the early Solar System experienced a long decline in asteroid impacts rather than a single catastrophic bombardment.".

Reconstructing Billions of Years of Asteroid Impacts.

Industry observers note that to investigate the Moon's bombardment history, the researchers examined tiny pieces of lunar rock for evidence of ancient collisions. Their analysis identified impact events dating from approximately 4.33 billion to 1.13 billion years ago, providing a record that spans more than three billion years.

According to recent reports, these findings offer a new perspective on how asteroid impacts changed over time. Rather than supporting the idea of a relatively brief period of exceptionally intense bombardment, the evidence points to a much longer process in which impacts became progressively less frequent.

Recent findings suggest that the implications extend beyond the Moon itself. According to Dr. Jourdan, reconstructing the history of lunar impacts can help scientists better understand the events that affected Earth during its earliest stages of development.

What Ancient Moon Rocks Reveal About Early Earth.

It has been revealed that "The Moon and Earth share a common history, but the evidence of early impacts has largely disappeared from our planet," Dr. Jourdan said.

"Because the Earth and Moon formed together, every major impact recorded on the Moon tells us something about the conditions experienced by the young Earth.

"Studying lunar rocks allows us to look back billions of years and better understand the events that shaped the environments of both worlds and helps us understand the role asteroid impacts played in planetary evolution and the conditions that may have influenced the emergence of life on Earth.

"The findings come amid a upcoming era of lunar exploration and science, with China's Chang'e-6 mission being the first to return samples from the Moon's far side.".

It has been revealed that the return of material from the lunar far side has given scientists an unprecedented opportunity to examine a region that was previously inaccessible to direct sampling. By comparing these rocks with samples from the Moon's near side, researchers can develop a more complete picture of the impacts that shaped the lunar surface and the wider Solar System.

The research was led by the State Key Laboratory of Deep Earth Processes and Resources at the Guangzhou Institute of Geochemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences.

The findings were published in Science Advances in a paper titled 'The bombardment history on the lunar farside revealed by 40Ar/39Ar geochronology of Chang'e-6 impact melt rocks'.

Materials provided by Curtin University. Original written by Lucien Wilkinson. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ariana Grande is addressing the online public discourse that erupted following the release of her “Petal” music video, admitting the commentary felt akin to Black Mirror and she hoped it would be received as her “sharing a vulnerable thing.”.
  • Sources indicate that the Oscar nominee appeared on Bowen Yang and Matt Rogers’ Las Culturistas podcast Wednesday, where they discussed the video for the title track of her eighth studio album Petal.
  • It’s like, the distortion is not your own.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ariana Grande is addressing the online public discourse that erupted following the release of her “Petal” music video, admitting the commentary felt akin to Black Mirror and she hoped it would be received as her “sharing a vulnerable thing.”.

Sources indicate that the Oscar nominee appeared on Bowen Yang and Matt Rogers’ Las Culturistas podcast Wednesday, where they discussed the video for the title track of her eighth studio album Petal. Yang brought up the character Grande plays in the video, an auditioning actress named Pepper who uses a chainsaw to kill people in the end after receiving repeated criticism from those she’s auditioning for, and stated: “There’s something about that that is so modern about someone in your position or really anyone who is being told to be more authentic.” Related Stories Movies 'Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' to Dominate Thanksgiving Box Office as 'Focker In-Law,' 'Hexed' Join Fray Movies 'Focker-in-Law' Filmmaker John Hamburg Talks Ariana Grande's Comedic Timing and the Actor Who Made Ben Stiller Laugh Hardest on Set.

“But that’s the distortion, right? It’s like, the distortion is not your own. It was given to you. It was by another’s hand,” the former Saturday Night Live star added, as the singer responded, “It’s kind of like, oh, when will it be about the art?”.

Recent findings suggest that “When will it be about the work? That was largely what the video was about is like, oh, here comes this girl, and there’s always some distortion around the performance or art, whatever it is,” Grande added.

Grande, Yang and Rogers spoke more about Pepper’s evolution as a character by the end of the video, as they shifted into discussing the public reaction to the video, which at the time heavily centered around her body.

Industry observers note that “It was a fun thing for then that video with the intention of really spelling it out,” Grande mentioned as Yang added, “got its own meta test it on.” The Focker-in-Law actress agreed, continuing, “had its own meta insane perception, and that was just really interesting. But I feel so proud and grateful. I wouldn’t change a thing. I would put it out again today exactly as is. I wouldn’t change a thing. I think my experience of putting art out and having people receive it is so different than how it used to be even just a few years ago.”.

Industry observers note that grande announced in August that she’d be taking a step back from the public eye following the finishing of her Eternal Sunshine Tour. “Ariana will be taking a step back from visibility after she completes the Eternal Sunshine Tour,” a statement shared with The Hollywood Reporter read.

“She looks forward to finishing the tour and ending it on a high note, both healthily and happily, and then taking a much-deserved break from public-facing work and appearances, which has led to endless, ongoing public scrutiny,” the statement continued. “This tour has been a beautiful experience for her. She loves her fans and has loved every minute of this tour so much.”.

Sources indicate that A source close to Grande also told THR at the time that her album Petal is “a fight song.” They added that it’s an “anthem about the love-hate relationship with the public and their toxicity. This album is not about any romantic partner or breakup in that way.” She also exited the West End revival of Sunday in the Park With George, which was later axed completely after Jonathan Bailey also dropped the project.

On Las Culturistas, Rogers asked Grande if she thinks that she “achieved something even more because of that conversation” that sparked online because “what you set out to do with the album [was] to make a comment about that, and then it had its own meta conversation.” He added, “Or does it feel like it really impacted and maybe commenting on that phenomenon to see that phenomenon happen as a result of the comment?”.

According to recent reports, “It’s Black Mirror,” Grande said. “It’s so funny and Black Mirror and bizarre. I really thought it was going to be a reveal, like me sharing a vulnerable — like, OK, here’s this thing. And then it happened and then sometimes 10 back. It was very funny and weird, but like I said, I love that project. I love that video.”.

The Grammy winner continued, “Those are two of my favorite videos, ‘Hate That I Made You Love Me’ and ‘Petal.’ I remember how it felt to be in the room, too, with all of those women dancers and all of us discussing what it felt like and what it held for us and we’ve all been told some kind of interesting thing about ourselves that has nothing to do with the art or our talent or our work or what we’ve given to our audition or whatever. That has nothing to do with anything.”.

Grande is currently starring in Focker-in-Law alongside Robert De Niro and Ben Stiller.

A galactic shock wave could rewrite the map of the Milky Way

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1183 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that latest research suggests the Milky Way produces stars in an unexpected location, revealing a surprising difference between our galaxy and most of its neighbors.
  • Industry observers note that the discovery comes from research led by a University of Sydney PhD student, who found evidence that a massive rotating structure of stars near the galactic center is generating powerful shock waves through surrounding clouds of gas.
  • Published in Nature Astronomy, the study also casts doubt on the nature of the Norma spiral arm, a feature of the Milky Way named for the constellation Norma as seen from Earth.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that latest research suggests the Milky Way produces stars in an unexpected location, revealing a surprising difference between our galaxy and most of its neighbors. The findings also raise questions about a familiar feature of the Milky Way, suggesting that part of what astronomers have long considered a spiral arm may actually be something else.

Industry observers note that the discovery comes from research led by a University of Sydney PhD student, who found evidence that a massive rotating structure of stars near the galactic center is generating powerful shock waves through surrounding clouds of gas. These waves squeeze the gas together, creating conditions that allow latest stars to form in a region where such intense forces usually prevent their birth.

Published in Nature Astronomy, the study also casts doubt on the nature of the Norma spiral arm, a feature of the Milky Way named for the constellation Norma as seen from Earth.

Lead author Dr. Hillary Davis, who recently completed her PhD at the University of Sydney's School of Physics and Sydney Institute for Astronomy, noted the research provides new insights into the structures near the galactic center and how gas moves around them.

Sources indicate that "At its heart, star formation is a process we understand from everyday physics. Forces set matter in motion. In this case gas is compressed, and that compression can create the conditions for fresh stars to be born on a massive scale," Dr. Davis mentioned.

Industry observers note that "In most similar galaxies, star formation very commonly occurs along spiral arms. What's extraordinary is seeing this happen in a different region of our Galaxy, where shocks are usually so strong that star formation is often suppressed.".

A Hidden Star Factory at the Heart of the Milky Way.

The Milky Way belongs to a class of galaxies known as barred spiral galaxies. Unlike galaxies with only a central concentration of stars and surrounding spiral arms, these systems contain an elongated structure of stars stretching across their central region. In our galaxy, this structure is called the Galactic bar.

Sources indicate that as the bar rotates, its gravity influences nearby gas, driving it into powerful shock fronts. These fronts compress the gas in much the same way that a shock wave compresses air.

Studying this structure from Earth is particularly difficult because we are located inside the Milky Way rather than viewing it from the outside. Large amounts of cosmic dust also block our view of the galactic center.

Industry observers note that "The Galactic bar cannot be easily observed because of a combination of our position in the Galaxy and dust obscuring our view," Dr. Davis mentioned.

"As a result, the bar's properties have been highly debated.".

Observations of other barred galaxies have shown that these shock fronts generally inhibit the formation of newly introduced stars, even in regions containing abundant gas. The intense conditions make it difficult for the gas to collapse into stars.

In a recent development, however, the latest findings indicate that the Milky Way may behave differently. Although it is not the only known example, our galaxy appears to belong to a relatively small group in which substantial star formation takes place along the shock fronts of the central bar.

"We believe that the Milky Way's bar has star formation occurring along its shock front, which is uncommon for most bars in nearby galaxies," Dr. Davis said.

A Milky Way Spiral Arm May Not Be What It Seems.

To investigate this unusual activity, the research team compared detailed computer simulations showing how galaxies change over billions of years with astronomical observations of regions where massive stars are forming.

In a recent development, A crucial part of the evidence came from masers, naturally occurring sources that emit highly concentrated microwave radiation. These emissions are associated with the formation of massive stars and operate on a principle similar to lasers, but at microwave wavelengths.

By examining the positions of these masers, the researchers uncovered a striking match between actual observations and the locations of shock fronts predicted by their simulations.

Industry observers note that "We found that masers previously associated with the Norma arm closely align with the shock front predicted by our simulations," Dr. Davis said. "This suggests that at least part of the so-called Norma arm may not be a spiral arm at all, but a region of star formation along the leading edge of the Galactic bar.

"This raises questions about the Galaxy's spiral structure, and the bar region of the Milky Way, which needs further investigation," she mentioned.

It has been revealed that the possibility is significant because it suggests that some of the star formation previously attributed to the Norma spiral arm could instead be occurring along the central bar. If confirmed, this interpretation would change how astronomers understand the arrangement of stars and gas in that part of the Milky Way.

Fresh Evidence Could Redraw the Milky Way's Map.

Beyond revealing an unusual location for star birth, the research also sheds light on the physical properties of the Galactic bar itself.

Astronomers have debated the structure's length, orientation, and rotation speed for decades, partly because the Milky Way's dust and our viewing position make direct measurements so challenging.

According to recent reports, "Our findings place further constraints on the size, angle and rotation speed of this central bar," Dr. Davis said.

The team's analysis indicates that the bar extends approximately 4.3 kiloparsecs, equivalent to about 14,000 light-years, outward from the galactic center along its long axis. This supports a picture of the Milky Way containing a relatively long bar that rotates slowly.

According to recent reports, the results illustrate how increasingly sophisticated simulations can help scientists investigate regions of our galaxy that are difficult to observe directly. By comparing models spanning billions of years with the available astronomical evidence, researchers can narrow down the possible structures and processes shaping the Milky Way.

"By comparing a new generation of large-scale computerized galaxy simulations, evolving over billions of years, against a more limited set of observations, we now have a stronger understanding of the bar and star formation processes in the Milky Way," Dr. Davis mentioned.

Sources indicate that the authors reported no competing interests. Research funding came from the Australian Research Council, the Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation, the Swedish Research Council, the Swedish National Space Agency, the LMK Foundation and eSSENCE (Sweden).

Computing resources and data storage were provided through National Computing Infrastructure Australia, an NCRIS capability supported by the Australian Government, and LUNARC, the Centre for Scientific and Technical Computing at Lund University, Sweden.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

EU enlargement: Why do some EU member states use their vetoes to block the accession of certain candidate countries?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1053 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's been quite a while since the European Union's last enlargement, when Croatia joined the bloc back in 2013.
  • If everything goes according to plan, another might soon be on the cards: Montenegro, with a population of just 620,000, could complete accession negotiations in the coming months and join the EU in early 2028.
  • But no sooner had EU Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos made this announcement in October than news emerged that Croatia might veto Montenegro's accession unless the country meets a series of Croatian demands.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's been quite a while since the European Union's last enlargement, when Croatia joined the bloc back in 2013.

If everything goes according to plan, another might soon be on the cards: Montenegro, with a population of just 620,000, could complete accession negotiations in the coming months and join the EU in early 2028.

But no sooner had EU Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos made this announcement in October than news emerged that Croatia might veto Montenegro's accession unless the country meets a series of Croatian demands. EU politicians and MEPs were dismayed.

This is not the first time something like this has happened: The veto rights that member states have on many EU matters have increasingly been used by individual countries in recent years as a means of leverage or obstruction, paralyzing the EU in the process.

DW takes a look at some of the most significant cases, the background to them and what are — in some instances — the serious political consequences of them.

In a recent development, montenegro is the most advanced EU candidate country, with a potential accession date of 2028. It has already provisionally closed several of the EU's 33 negotiating chapters.

As of November 23, however, Croatia is blocking the closure of three chapters that have already been negotiated.

Zagreb is demanding, among other things, compensation for former prisoners held in Montenegrin camps during the Yugoslav wars of the 1990s, clarification of the fate of Croatians who have been missing since that time, and more rigorous prosecution of war crimes.

In a recent development, there are also disputes over the precise maritime boundary between the two countries. In addition, Croatia is demanding payment of about €2.4 billion (about $2.6 billion) for assets that belonged to the Yugoslav People's Army, the army of the former Yugoslavia to which both countries belonged before its breakup in the early 1990s.

Montenegro has already responded to some of Croatia's demands, including those concerning compensation for former prisoners. Others, such as the one relating to the assets of the Yugoslav People's Army, are disputed.

Sources indicate that it is clear that Croatia's list of demands is also driven by domestic politics. No government in Zagreb can afford to appear compliant on concerns relating to the Croatian War of Independence (1991–95).

Moreover, moderate conservative Prime Minister Andrej Plenkovic, who is regularly accused in Croatia of being too pro-EU, can use the dispute to portray himself as a staunch defender of national interests.

After Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the EU in June 2022 granted Ukraine and the Republic of Moldova EU candidate status through an accelerated procedure as a gesture of solidarity.

Sources indicate that many EU member states have reservations about Ukraine joining the bloc quickly. Nevertheless, only Hungary, under former Prime Minister Viktor Orban, adopted an obstructive stance.

Industry observers note that ostensibly, Hungary's obstruction was about getting Ukraine to improve the rights of the Hungarian minority in Transcarpathia in western Ukraine. But Orban used the matter for domestic political purposes and as an election campaign issue, portraying Ukraine as a "mafia state.".

In an effort to appeal to widespread anti-Ukrainian sentiment in Hungary, the country's new prime minister, Peter Magyar, has also adopted a tough stance on Ukraine.

Nevertheless, Magyar's government lifted several temporary blocks on the opening of new negotiating chapters after the Ukrainian parliament passed a law in early October strengthening the educational rights of national minorities.

No EU candidate country has suffered as much or as long from veto politics as North Macedonia: It was granted EU candidate status in 2005 but only began accession negotiations in July 2022.

Greece blocked the start of negotiations for 13 years because it objected to the name "Republic of Macedonia," as the country was previously known, and accused its neighbor of laying territorial claims to the region of Macedonia in northern Greece.

The dispute was settled in 2018 through a compromise that saw the country change its name to the Republic of North Macedonia the following year.

But just as the path to accession negotiations seemed clear, Bulgaria blocked the opening of talks in November 2020.

Bulgaria regards the Macedonian language as a dialect of Bulgarian and disputes the existence of a distinct Macedonian nation.

Here, too, domestic Bulgarian politics is ultimately a factor.

Former Bulgarian President and current Prime Minister Rumen Radev, for example, fueled the escalation with North Macedonia to enhance his political profile.

Although Serbia has been negotiating EU accession since 2014, little progress has been made.

In July, when the country was still led by President Aleksandar Vucic, no less than eight EU member states — including Croatia — opposed opening further negotiating chapters with Serbia.

While the main reservations relate to democratic shortcomings, deficiencies in the rule of law and corruption in Serbia, Croatia also has its own disputes with its eastern neighbor.

These concern the 1991–95 war, including missing persons, war crimes, minority rights and differing interpretations of history. Relations are also strained by nationalist rhetoric on both sides.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Whether the election victory of the Student List in Belgrade in late October , after almost two years of anti-government and anti-corruption protests, will change this situation is impossible to say.

The EU opened accession negotiations with Albania, which has been an EU candidate since 2014, in July 2022.

Recent findings suggest that albania could become the bloc's next fresh member after Montenegro. However, Greece has repeatedly threatened (most recently in June) to block the accession process unless the rights of its Greek minority, particularly their property rights, are adequately protected.

In light of all this, Brussels has long been debating a reform of the accession process and the EU veto system.

Recent findings suggest that in early October, the European Commission proposed that decisions to open negotiations with candidate countries be made by qualified majority rather than unanimously. It also proposed that newly introduced EU members would be required to give up the right to veto decisions in certain policy areas altogether for a specified period.

The problem with these proposed reforms is that they would themselves have to be adopted unanimously. In other words, any member state could veto the reform.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Engineers and analysts searching for the root cause of the technical issues behind Friday's nationwide ground stop by the Federal Aviation Administration have been able to replicate the situation that was overwhelming parts of the air traffic system, people familiar with the investigation told CNBC.

Sources indicate that while replicating the issue in a lab in Florida is progress, those investigating the matter have yet to determine exactly why two routers in question failed, according to the people, who requested anonymity to talk about an ongoing situation. Finding the root cause is critical to the FAA determining if there may be an issue with other routers that form the backbone of communications for the national air transportation network.

The ground stop lasted for more than four hours Friday, marking the longest halt to U.S. flight departures since 9/11.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford have said there is no indication the routers failed due to a cyberattack.

The incident in question happened shortly after L3Harris Technologies, the primary contractor supporting the FAA telecommunications network, installed a newly introduced router at a facility in El Dorado, Arkansas.

L3Harris noted that it, in partnership with other tech companies, has completed more than 70% of the planned airspace communications conversion from legacy copper wires to a fiber-optic system.

"We are supporting the FAA in its investigation to understand the conditions that led to the Nov. 13 ground stop of our nation's air travel," the statement noted. "L3Harris takes the nationwide ground stop and its impact on travelers, airlines and air traffic operations seriously.".

Investigators said within eight minutes of its installation, the router began to transmit too much data within the FAA network.

That surge of data, 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds, destabilized aircraft communications and radar feeds, Duffy said.

Since the ground stop, Duffy has increased the amount of money he wants to upgrade the national air traffic system. After originally asking for $30 billion to build a digital network that will incorporate artificial intelligence, Duffy has now asked Congress for $50 billion.

In a sea of Israeli flags, Yiftach Golov holds one that looks a little different.

Among the hundreds of thousands of protesters who took to the streets for the 13th week in a row on Saturday, Golov hoists a brown flag that represents a group called “Brother and Sisters in Arms.”.

They are veterans – many, like Golov, from elite forces – who now feel they are fighting on a newly introduced battlefield: To save Israeli democracy.

“We believe this is our responsibility to go once again called to the flag of the nation to stop this madness to defend Israel,” Golov said, as he weaved his way through the protesters on Tel Aviv’s Kaplan street, between the high-rises that house many of Israel’s high tech companies.

During the second intifada, in the early 2000s, Golov served in a special forces reconnaissance unit. He was never before particularly political, focusing more on getting his PhD in biophysics from Tel Aviv University.

But when the protest movement against the Israeli government’s judicial overhaul initiative began in January, Golov attended one a demonstration and soon became one of thousands of veterans, and now military reservists, who have taken up the cause as their fresh mission.

Some, including elite Air Force reservists, have taken it a step further, threatening not to heed the call to train or even serve in protest of the government’s plans planned judicial changes, which would give the governing parties more control over Israel’s judiciary.

According to recent reports, others have taken to becoming some of the most active organizers and demonstrators. Last week, a group from Brothers and Sisters in Arms protested by carrying a figure wrapped in the Israeli flag on a stretcher, the way they would carry a wounded comrade off the field.

While Golov notes he has not taken the drastic step to refuse service, he understands the motivation.

According to recent reports, “We’re fighting for justice and liberty, just like the American story, that’s the values that that are being represented symbolized back when we look at our flag, that’s something that was lacking lacking for the last few decades. So basically, we reclaim the flag,” he mentioned.

Palestinian taxi driver recounts surviving attack by right-wing protesters.

According to recent reports, fellow members of the group, all wearing brown shirts with the organization’s logo, come up and say hello. They’re sprinkled all throughout the protests. One is even leading the “Pink Front,” a group of coordinated drummers who look like they are dressed for a rave, and often lead the chants at the protests.

Sources indicate that they’re using skills they learned in the military – how to organize, how to mobilize – now for the protests. But more importantly, they say they have the same type of motivation.

“The very deep feeling that you are part of something bigger than yourself, that (you’re) allowed to sacrifice anything that is needed, whether it’s your career, health, seriously mental health,” Golov said. “We all have a mission, you’re willing to do it at any cost. You’re very determined, you know that you are on the right side, you’re carrying the torch of light. That keeps us being highly motivated despite the fact that we’re not sleeping for days.”.

Israel’s protest movement is made up of many disparate groups, but the pressure from Israel’s much vaunted veterans has been seen as a key to moving the needle.

Last Monday, after weeks of sustained protests and the largest general strike in Israeli history, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced a pause to the legislation, to allow time for negotiations with the opposition.

Industry observers note that but despite the announcements, protesters are still out in the streets in large numbers. CNN affiliate Channel 12 in Israel estimated the size of Saturday’s demonstration in Tel Aviv at about 150,000 people. Organizers claimed it was 230,000.

Last week’s mass protests and widespread strike action came after Netanyahu remarked he had decided to fire Defense Minister Yoav Gallant for advocating a delay in passing the legislation – a move that Netanyahu has since delayed, sources told CNN, due to “the present security situation.”.

Sources indicate that in his televised speech calling for a delay, Gallant had said the pause in the legislation was needed “for the security of Israel,” citing the refusal of some Israel Defense Forces reservists to train in protest of the government prepares. He said pressing ahead with the proposals could threaten Israel’s security.

Under pressure at home and from allies abroad, Netanyahu stated he would delay votes on the remaining legislation until after the Knesset’s Passover recess in April “to give time for a real chance for a real debate.”.

“Out of the responsibility to the nation, I decided to delay … the vote, in order to give time for discussion,” he added.

It has been revealed that but Netanyahu indicated that the delay was only temporary. He insisted that the overhaul was necessary, and reiterated criticism of refusal to train or serve in the military in protest at the planned changes. “Refusing is the end of our country,” he mentioned.

Many protesters don’t believe that the pause is real, or say it’s simply a stalling tactic to give Netanyahu some breathing room and get the protesters to go home before he plows on with the reforms.

“We will start doing deactivation only when we will know 100% that Israel state will stay a functional democratic country. Whatever needs to be done for that,” Golov noted.

A black hole the size of an atom could destroy an entire star

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Some of the smallest black holes ever proposed may be capable of destroying entire stars from the inside.
  • Sources indicate that researchers at MIT and other institutions have now identified a possible way to find them.
  • Their study, published in The Astrophysical Journal, describes a remarkable possibility.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some of the smallest black holes ever proposed may be capable of destroying entire stars from the inside. Scientists believe these mysterious objects, known as primordial black holes, could have formed during the first fraction of a second after the Big Bang, when extremely dense regions of matter collapsed under their own gravity. If they exist, these ancient remnants could also account for a substantial portion of dark matter, the invisible material that makes up most of the matter in the universe.

Sources indicate that researchers at MIT and other institutions have now identified a possible way to find them. Using theoretical calculations and computer simulations in three dimensions, the team investigated what would happen if a primordial black hole became trapped inside a star similar to our Sun.

Their study, published in The Astrophysical Journal, describes a remarkable possibility. A black hole no larger than an atom, but carrying the mass of an asteroid, could gradually sink toward the center of a star and begin consuming it from within.

In a recent development, if the star rotates rapidly enough, material falling toward the black hole would eventually form a spinning disk around it. That development could set the stage for a catastrophic explosion.

"Once the disk forms, this is essentially a death sentence for the star," claims lead author Ore Gottlieb, an assistant professor of physics at MIT.

According to recent reports, the interaction between the black hole and the surrounding disk could produce enormous jets of matter that punch through the star and cause it to explode within seconds. Researchers predict that the resulting outburst would emit intense blue and ultraviolet light, along with X-rays and gamma rays, potentially making it visible to telescopes already in operation.

"There is hope for us to probe primordial black holes through interactions with stars," Gottlieb notes. "We expect this to be visible, and it's something we should look into.".

The research team also included Matteo Cantiello of the Flatiron Institute, Cameron Norton and Matthew Kleban of Fresh York University, and Ken Van Tilburg of Stanford University.

Ancient Black Holes That May Have Survived the Big Bang.

According to recent reports, not every primordial black hole formed in the early universe would still exist today. According to a theory developed by physicist Stephen Hawking, black holes gradually lose energy through a quantum process called Hawking radiation. Over immense periods of time, this process causes them to shrink, and the smallest primordial black holes would already have evaporated completely.

Heavier primordial black holes, however, could have survived to the present day. Some might be approximately the size of an atom while containing as much mass as an asteroid (or about a millionth of the mass of the Earth).

These extraordinary objects raise an intriguing question. If they are still scattered throughout the universe, what would happen when one encounters a star? More importantly, could the resulting interaction provide the evidence needed to establish that primordial black holes actually exist?

Industry observers note that to investigate, Gottlieb and his colleagues combined mathematical calculations with numerical simulations incorporating general relativity, fluid dynamics, stellar evolution, and particle physics. Their goal was to understand how a primordial black hole could become trapped by a star and what would happen afterward.

How a Tiny Black Hole Could Become Trapped Inside a Star.

Industry observers note that the researchers found that a star acting alone generally could not capture a primordial black hole passing nearby. Its gravitational attraction would be insufficient to keep the black hole from escaping.

Recent findings suggest that the situation changes when another object is involved. A companion star or planet could alter the gravitational interaction enough to allow the primordial black hole to become trapped.

In this arrangement involving three objects, the black hole could repeatedly travel through the star. Each passage would create friction as it moved through stellar material, gradually draining energy from its orbit and drawing it closer to the star's center.

In a recent development, the process could take thousands or even millions of years. Although that sounds extraordinarily slow, it is relatively brief compared with the age of the universe.

Eventually, the black hole would settle into the star's core, where it could begin feeding on the surrounding material.

"Then, this is where the action begins," Gottlieb says.

A Black Hole Could Slowly Consume a Star From Within.

According to recent reports, once the primordial black hole reaches the stellar core, its growth depends partly on what happens to the energy generated as gas falls toward it. Some of that energy can heat the surrounding material, potentially slowing the rate at which additional gas falls inward.

Sources indicate that the team's simulations indicate that most of the energy would instead disappear into the black hole. This would allow it to accumulate matter more rapidly than earlier estimates suggested.

Over several million years, the growing black hole could consume approximately 1 percent of the star's total mass. At that stage, its fate would depend heavily on how quickly the star rotates.

According to recent reports, if the star spins fast enough, gas would no longer be able to plunge directly into the black hole. Instead, the material would gather into a rotating disk around the black hole, which would by then have grown to several meters in size.

Recent findings suggest that "Inside the star, you have a black hole with a disk," Gottlieb claims. "The black hole is also spinning, and it's twisting space and time.".

As the disk continues feeding the black hole, the extreme rotation twists the magnetic field threading the surrounding material. This process could generate exceptionally powerful jets that shoot outward from the black hole's poles.

Sources indicate that "This twisted magnetic field will power very strong electromagnetic jets from the poles of the black hole," Gottlieb explains. "And these jets will just explode the star, within a few dozen seconds. It's very fast. Once you have a disk, you are done.".

What began as a tiny black hole hidden inside an otherwise ordinary star could therefore end in a violent explosion, with the star's destruction unfolding in a matter of seconds once the critical conditions are reached.

Exploding Stars Could Reveal Primordial Black Holes and Dark Matter.

The researchers also calculated what these unusual explosions might look like to astronomers, estimating how their brightness and color would change across different wavelengths of light.

According to recent reports, their models predict a recognizable sequence of emissions, beginning with high-energy radiation and progressing through other parts of the electromagnetic spectrum as the explosion evolves. The initial outburst could include intense blue and ultraviolet light, along with gamma rays and X-rays.

Sources indicate that "We would initially detect some X-rays and gamma rays, then over time optical and infrared emissions, and later on radio emissions," Gottlieb notes. "This is something we could potentially detect, if it's not happening too far from us. It could be many galaxies away, not just in our backyard.".

Such signals could be detectable with existing astronomical instruments, potentially allowing researchers to search for primordial black holes far beyond the Milky Way.

However, identifying one would not be straightforward. Other cosmic events can generate similar flashes of radiation, so an unusual explosion alone would not establish that a primordial black hole was responsible.

According to recent reports, astronomers would need to examine additional evidence, including the characteristics of the exploding star. One especially revealing clue would be an explosion involving a star that would not ordinarily be expected to meet such a violent end.

According to recent reports, "For instance, if the star is a certain mass that is not supposed to explode, it must be something that is happening inside that is a sort of parasite that is consuming the star from the inside," Gottlieb says. "The broader impact is that we can now place constraints on primordial black holes, and their contributions to dark matter, using observations.".

Even if no convincing examples are found, the search could help scientists determine how common primordial black holes might be and how much dark matter they could account for.

In a recent development, for now, primordial black holes remain hypothetical. But the new research offers astronomers a possible observational signature to pursue, connecting the spectacular destruction of stars with objects that may have existed since the universe's earliest moments.

The research received partial support from the U.S. Department of Energy Office of Science Advanced Scientific Computing Research Program and the National Science Foundation.

Zyri, who voiced the titular character in “Steven Universe” and played Brian Corbett on “The Goldbergs,” has come out as trans. In a Substack post on Wednesday, Zyri wrote about the challenges of being a child star and coming to terms with their gender identity.

“Coming to terms with my dysphoria and my transness was only a small piece of my journey towards being a whole, authentic person, but it was notable as the first thing that truly felt like mine in my entire life,” Zyri wrote. “That’s also why for a time I was so terrified of being outed: I didn’t want to lose my newfound light the way I’d lost control of my name, my childhood, and my entire identity to the brand I was molded into by others. I know now that I really had nothing to fear there — the only thing that defines me is me — but I’ve had to continuously unlearn being afraid of losing all of myself again. That’s probably something I’ll have to remind myself of for the rest of my life, but at least now, for the very first time, I can envision the rest of my life. I celebrated my twenty-eighth birthday just over a year ago now, and the symbolic nature of that number shouldn’t be lost on anyone who grew up like I did. What twenty-one year old me would’ve cynically viewed as being past my cosmically-assigned expiration date, is now something that truly feels worth celebrating. To any of you poor souls who had to suffer my angst-riddled but still disconcertingly genuine former aspirations to wrap my life up at twenty-seven, I’m terribly sorry, and am also happy to report that I didn’t even come close to sticking the landing.” Related Stories Vatican-Produced Doc 'Green Lava' Drops Trailer Featuring Justin Bieber's 'Everything Hallelujah' (EXCLUSIVE) Ariana Grande Indicates 'Petal' Music Video Backlash Felt Like 'Black Mirror' and 'I Wouldn’t Change a Thing. I'd Put It Out Again Today As Is'.

Industry observers note that zyri voiced Steven Universe and several other characters on the Cartoon Network series across all five seasons and 160 episodes, in addition to a TV movie, a follow-up series and several video games. Zyri’s TV debut came in 2009 on “Are You Smarter Than a Fifth Grader?,” and they also appeared in episodes of “Hannah Montana,” “iCarly,” “Fresh Off the Boat,” “Henry Danger” and animated titles like “The Legend of Korra,” “Justice League: War,” “Batman: The Long Halloween, Part Two,” “Injustice” and many more. Zyri also gave an enhancement that they have been married for a year and will “wade back into” performing after not appearing in a live-action project since 2019 and an animated role since 2024.

In a recent development, “As for the future, my hope is that not too much changes in my daily life going forward,” Zyri wrote. “I do genuinely love and miss performing and creating, though it’s only very recently that I’ve felt well enough to wade back into it. I recognize that my job often requires some degree of public visibility, but for the foreseeable future I intend to only engage in that when it’s necessary, rather than proactively. I do place an extremely high value on privacy these days, and while there will always be some blurring of the lines between personal and professional life, I’m very happy to have actually separated the two for the first time and I don’t wish to give that up again. Being a child performer has a way of capturing your psychological development and splicing those two pieces together until they’re simply the same thing; everything I’ve written about overcoming here could be summed up as the process of carefully untangling them from each other until they’re the way they ought to be.”.

Breaking: Mysterious new viruses reveal a missing link in evolution

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1103 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Researchers at the University of Miami have discovered a previously unknown group of viruses that could help explain a missing piece of evolutionary history.
  • According to recent reports, the research, published in Nature Communications, challenges the conventional explanation for the origins of cellular structures known as encapsulins.
  • The discovery could have vital implications for biotechnology and for understanding the origins and early evolution of life.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Researchers at the University of Miami have discovered a previously unknown group of viruses that could help explain a missing piece of evolutionary history. The finding reveals an unexpected connection between viruses and tiny protein compartments inside cells, offering latest clues about how some of life's earliest biological structures may have developed.

According to recent reports, the research, published in Nature Communications, challenges the conventional explanation for the origins of cellular structures known as encapsulins. Scientists previously believed these compartments evolved from viruses. However, the latest evidence suggests a more complicated evolutionary relationship in which viruses and encapsulins may have repeatedly evolved from one another over millions of years.

The discovery could have vital implications for biotechnology and for understanding the origins and early evolution of life. It also raises the possibility that viruses have biological functions that scientists have largely overlooked.

Mysterious Upcoming Viruses Reveal an Evolutionary Connection.

Sources indicate that at the center of the discovery are proteins that fold into a distinctive three-dimensional structure known as the HK97-fold. These proteins can assemble into protective shells and are found in both viruses and encapsulins.

The newly identified viruses have smaller, simpler genomes than other viruses that produce HK97-fold protein shells. They also possess characteristics associated with both viruses and encapsulins, making them possible evolutionary intermediates between the two. Studying these unusual viruses could help researchers understand how increasingly complex biological systems first appeared.

"What makes the HK97-fold proteins so interesting is that they can form shells that enclose biochemical reactions in cellular lineages, archaea, and bacteria. But they also serve genetic purposes in viruses, storing and protecting their viral genome," noted Abelardo Aguilar, the study's first author and a Ph.D. student in the Department of Biology at the University of Miami College of Arts and Sciences.

"These proteins build compartments with two different roles, which connects directly with the study of the origin of life and its early evolution because if you think about it, life at its core is about enclosing reactions and also enclosing information that can be inherited so those reactions can happen in the future.".

AI Helps Discover Hidden Viruses in Billions of DNA Sequences.

It has been revealed that to uncover these previously unknown viruses, Aguilar worked with Antoni Luque Santolaria, the study's senior author and an associate professor in the Department of Biology. Luque also holds secondary appointments in the Department of Physics within the College of Arts and Sciences and the Department of Chemical, Environmental and Materials Engineering in the College of Engineering. The project brought together collaborators from multiple institutions.

Rather than relying on laboratory experiments to grow viruses, the team searched enormous genetic databases containing billions of DNA sequences. They combined bioinformatics, models of protein behavior, and artificial intelligence tools, including protein language models and AlphaFold, to investigate the structures encoded by these sequences.

In a recent development, the databases included IMG/M, a resource associated with the U.S. Department of Energy's Joint Genome Institute and the University of California, Berkeley. Its genetic information comes from environmental samples collected around the world, including soil, seawater, wastewater, the human gut, and numerous other locations.

This approach allows scientists to investigate viruses that have never been successfully grown in a laboratory, greatly expanding the number of organisms and evolutionary relationships they can study.

Sources indicate that "The majority of viruses cannot be grown in the lab. But now through sequencing, we have access to information on viruses for which we don't know the host, that we can't culture in the lab, but that are everywhere," Luque explained. "That means there are multiple questions in relation to evolution and how viruses have adapted to the world that it's now possible to explore bioinformatically.".

Viral Protein Shells May Have Unexpected Functions.

Beyond identifying the new viruses, the researchers proposed a possible molecular explanation for how viruses and encapsulins could have evolved from one another.

According to recent reports, their model centers on procapsids, immature viral protein shells (capsids) that may provide a pathway between the two types of structures. These shells could potentially support both genetic functions, such as containing viral DNA, and metabolic functions involving chemical reactions.

It has been revealed that this raises an intriguing possibility. Viral capsids are generally recognized for packaging and protecting genetic material, but certain forms might also help create environments where biochemical reactions can occur.

"One implication of this research is the possibility that viral capsids could also facilitate biochemical reactions, which would open up the potential roles that capsids have in environments as a whole," Aguilar explained.

Although further research is needed to establish these potential functions, the findings suggest that scientists may need to look beyond the infectious stages of viruses to fully understand their roles in nature.

"When we're looking at viruses, we tend to look only at the particles that are infective, and this study points out that we might need to start putting more emphasis on the non-infective versions of the virus and what other functions those viral-like particles may have that we have overlooked in the past.".

New AI Tools Open the Door to More Viral Discoveries.

Sources indicate that the research also demonstrates how artificial intelligence and computational biology are transforming the study of viruses. By combining powerful analytical tools with knowledge of protein structure and physical behavior, scientists can now investigate evolutionary questions that were previously difficult to explore.

In a recent development, supported by the Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation and the U.S. National Science Foundation, the project provides a framework for studying other poorly understood viruses and their biological capabilities.

The researchers believe these methods could also be useful beyond evolutionary biology, including efforts to understand newly emerging viruses and pathogens.

In a recent development, "If you have the right question and you pair it with the right tools and physical insights, it gives researchers an opportunity to look at viruses in a way that we didn't have an opportunity to do before," Luque said. "There are evolution questions, but there are also questions about emerging pathogens or emerging viruses. The set of tools that we use can be moved forward in different contexts.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told employees on Tuesday that the tech giant’s code of conduct allows room for a “second chance,” that succession planning is a “flawed’ process,” and that he would work to rein in his “insanely intense” management style, according to remarks reviewed by WIRED.

In a recent development, during his first all-hands since returning as CEO, Huang acknowledged that he violated the organization’s policies and made some “very serious personal mistakes” that damaged his relationships with his wife and two children and prompted him to resign. But he stated Nvidia’s board of directors made the appropriate decision for the company in welcoming him back. He added that the board made that call, not “the highest levels of our government.”.

According to recent reports, huang spoke for about an hour, offering deeply personal thoughts about his therapy sessions and drawing applause at times from employees at Nvidia’s Silicon Valley headquarters as he spoke about the manufacturer’s success and future. He didn’t take any questions. While some Nvidia employees celebrated Huang’s return, others remained concerned about his behavior and the board’s decision to reinstate him.

It has been revealed that “This is going to be the hardest firm meeting I’ve ever done, and the second hardest meeting I have ever done,” Huang noted as he began to speak. “The hardest meeting I’ve ever done was with my wife.”.

Recent findings suggest that nvidia’s board accepted Huang’s resignation earlier this month, citing concerns about his personal behavior and lack of candor following news reports about extramarital affairs, including one with a woman accused of having ties to Chinese intelligence services. The very same board reinstated him on Monday, just 11 days later, after receiving fresh assurances from Huang and learning from the Trump administration that he was not under federal criminal scrutiny and his return would not be a risk to national security.

Huang and Nvidia, though, continue to face other legal and regulatory challenges. The board is investigating whether he was the target of foreign intelligence. US lawmakers expect him to testify before Congress next week. Lawsuits and other probes are ongoing into Nvidia’s disclosures about Huang’s behavior and its compliance with US export controls on chips.

Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Sources indicate that huang told staffers that he has been going to therapy “every day for an hour and a half” and that it’s “been helping me a lot.” He added that he “made some very serious personal mistakes. I hurt my family, I hurt my wife.”.

While Huang said he had never knowingly made a decision contrary to the firm’s interests, he conceded that “in this one area” he had lacked “the courage” to disclose information that he knew would hurt his family, seemingly referring to the extramarital affairs.

“The board and I spent the whole weekend together, and they, of course, they've been contemplating, and they've been collecting facts,” Huang mentioned. “They came to the judgment that they would like to invite me back as the CEO, to give me a second chance.”.

The CEO emphasized that Nvidia’s code of conduct, much of which he remarked he wrote himself, still governs how employees are expected to treat one another and is intended to “create an environment that’s safe for people.”.

Industry observers note that huang told employees that violations of the code would not be tolerated. But that “does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door,” he noted. “Facts, circumstances, a lot of assessments” would factor in.

Recent findings suggest that “It has to always be evaluated in the context of the human,” he said. “And this firm has been more than gracious, more than thoughtful, more than fair in giving me a second chance.”.

Huang also pushed back against the notion that he had received preferential treatment because of his status in Silicon Valley. “There are rumors on the internet that apparently I’m a tech bro, and therefore I’m back,” Huang remarked. He rejected the suggestion that he was above the law or Nvidia’s code of conduct.

Sources indicate that later in the meeting, Huang addressed criticism of his self-described “deeply intense, insanely intense” management style, acknowledging that his behavior had at times negatively affected employees. While Huang maintained that the intensity he brings to his job elevates those around him, he conceded that he sometimes takes things too far.

“It disempowers them, and that’s not right,” Huang stated. The Nvidia CEO said he needed to figure out how to maintain his level of dedication to the company without hurting the people who work there.

It has been revealed that “I need to hold myself to a higher standard at this time,” Huang noted. He said that he would undergo a 360-degree performance review, soliciting feedback as often as monthly from people who work with him. The CEO added that he would be the first and only person at Nvidia to undergo such a review and that he did not want to institute the practice companywide.

Recent findings suggest that huang acknowledged during the meeting that Trump was a vocal supporter of Nvidia but insisted that politics played no role in how the firm operated. “It is absolutely true that President Trump really, really loves our company,” Huang remarked. “He is my president. And I’ll do everything I can to help this president.”.

In a recent development, huang said he would take the same approach with future US presidents. “We are the most apolitical organization,” he said. “I don’t love that we talk about politics here. I love that we talk about work here.”.

Huang also sought to reassure women at Nvidia, describing himself as “one of our greatest advocates for creating an environment for women” and touting the firm’s flexible work policies, which he said allow employees to simultaneously build their families and careers.

“If I did anything that put that in jeopardy, I cannot tell you how sad I am, and I’ll do everything I can to fix it,” Huang said.

After Huang’s resignation, he and the organization’s board received criticism from Wall Street for not having an obvious internal successor in line. Huang addressed the matter head-on during the company meeting. “I don't believe in succession planning; I think it’s flawed,” he remarked, specifying that the concept may make sense but the implementation often causes challenges.

Huang described each of his 60 reports as CEOs of their own units who could step up when he eventually leaves. “It creates resilience, and it creates the opportunity, which is ultimately the responsibility of the board, to give them the opportunity to decide at that time what the world needed, what the company needed, and be able to choose from a large collection of amazing people,” he said.

The CEO also argued that his brief absence had demonstrated Nvidia’s ability to operate without him. “I promise you, whether I’m here or not, this manufacturer is wired up to execute, execute, and execute,” Huang mentioned.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie have settled a long-running dispute over the sale of their French winery, a lawsuit that opened the door for the actress to accuse her ex-husband of abusing her and their children.

Industry observers note that both sides on Wednesday moved to dismiss claims against each other. Terms of the settlement weren’t disclosed.

“We have settled out of court in the best interests of our family and will not be commenting further,” mentioned representatives for Jolie and Pitt in a statement. “Any comments in media stories attributed to ‘sources’ are in fact not coming from either of us, or anyone close to us.”.

The couple purchased the 1,200-acre winery in the South of France where they married, Château Miraval, in 2008. Jolie planned to sell her half to Pitt in the wake of their divorce, court filings alleged, until negotiations broke down over his insistence that she sign a nondisclosure agreement barring her from publicizing allegations of abuse leading up to their split.

Jolie balked at the ask and instead struck a $64 million deal with billionaire alcohol magnate Yuri Shefler for her half of the winery. Pitt in 2022 filed a lawsuit, claiming that the actress reneged on an unwritten agreement that they wouldn’t sell their stakes in the business without the other’s consent. That led to a countersuit from Jolie publicizing for the first time abuse allegations against Pitt in a 2016 altercation on a private plane in which she claimed that the actor “grabbed her by the head and shook her,” “choked one of the children” and “struck another in the face.”.

Recent findings suggest that at the time, a representative for Pitt denied the allegations. Jolie “continues to rehash, revise and reimagine her description of an event that happened 6 years ago by adding completely untrue information each time she fails to get what she wants,” the spokesperson stated. “Her story is constantly evolving.”.

Wednesday’s settlement ends a contentious case that peeled back the origins of Pitt and Jolie’s divorce and hostility between the former couple. Pitt continues to pursue claims against Shefler, who allegedly orchestrated the acquisition in secret alongside Jolie, and Shefler’s manufacturer Tenute del Mondo, the wine arm of the Stoli Group. The actor seeks a court order allowing him to purchase Jolie’s shares in Miraval at the same valuation Shefler acquired them, plus unspecified damages.

According to recent reports, A state appeals court earlier this year found that Shefler played a vital role in structuring and finalizing the deal to purchase Miraval. It pointed to him guaranteeing $39 million of the purchase using his own funds, a provision he wouldn’t agree to if he wasn’t involved in the agreement. Shefler sent three letters to Jolie over the course of the transaction, according to court filings. One thanked her for accepting his offer and assured her that a deal would be made “despite personal complications.” Another asked Jolie to postpone paying an installment on the purchase due to complications with Pitt.

Since the allegations became public in 2022, Pitt has continued starring in major studio productions, like F1 and Heart of the Beast, maintaining his dual-standing as one of Hollywood’s most bankable leading men and a prolific producer of prestige film through Proposal B Entertainment. Jolie, meanwhile, momentarily took a step back from acting before earning critical acclaim for her portrayal as Maria Callas in Maria.

In her cross complaint, Jolie detailed a physical altercation with Pitt, with him on one side and her and their children on the other.

Recent findings suggest that “Pitt lunged at his own child and Jolie grabbed him from behind to stop him,” the complaint stated. “To get Jolie off his back, Pitt threw himself backwards into the airplane’s seats injuring Jolie’s back and elbow. The children rushed in and all bravely tried to protect each other.”.

At one point, Pitt poured beer on Jolie; at another, he poured beer and wine on the children, the lawsuit alleged. Once the flight landed, Jolie claimed Pitt pushed her when she told him that she and the children were going to a hotel. “He also grabbed and shook Jolie by the head and shoulders, causing one of the children to beg, ‘Don’t hurt her,’” the complaint stated. “He let Jolie go, but then called her a ‘bitch,’ before adding, ‘Fuck you, fuck you all.’” Jolie filed for divorce five days later.

Industry observers note that the FBI investigated the 2016 altercation but declined to press charges. A redacted report on the case stated that the investigating agent found there was probable cause to pursue a criminal case but that charges would not be filed due to “several factors,” according to The Fresh York Times. It described Jolie as being “conflicted on whether or not to be supportive of charges.”.

Recent findings suggest that pitt is represented by John Berlinski and Julia Cherlow, partners at Bird Marella, while Jolie was represented by Paul Murphy and Daniel Csillag. Alejandro Brito, who handles media lawsuit for President Trump, represents Shefler.

That matter is not for the NATO Parliamentary Assembly, which was gathered for its 72nd annual meeting in Berlin, to decide. But it was key to the Ukrainian president to reiterate his request.

After the war ends, Ukraine needs strong security guarantees and NATO could ensure those. "Wouldn't it be more effective to simply bring Ukraine into NATO?" Zelenskyy asked, arguing: "Wouldn't that be better for all of us, for everyone? Cheaper to put in place? And more reliable when it comes to actually protecting security?".

According to recent reports, there is conflict among NATO members about the possibility of admitting Ukraine. The alliance has affirmed multiple times that the path to membership stands open to Ukraine — however, in the long term rather than the near future. This is primarily because of the ongoing war and the possible assistance obligations of other NATO countries for Ukraine, which was attacked by Russia.

NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte rejected the Ukrainian demands at the summit, which for the first time in 26 years was held in Berlin. Ukraine had entry prospects; however, NATO members at the moment lack unanimity on this problem. NATO alone decides who becomes a member. "There is total clarity on that within the alliance," Rutte remarked.

In a recent development, german Chancellor Friedrich Merz advocated for Ukraine to receive security guarantees similar to what NATO members have, in the instance of a possible ceasefire. In retrospect, it was clear "what a mistake it was not to follow the American suggestion back in 2008 at the NATO summit in Bucharest to admit Ukraine as a member," Merz said at a joint press conference following a meeting with Rutte.

Sources indicate that whether or not a NATO entry for Ukraine could be part of negotiations with Russia is another question, according to Rutte. He approved of current US efforts to bring about peace talks, and how Europe was closely consulting with Ukraine and the US for a unified position. "But it is also to test now whether Putin is willing to play ball, and then these issues might come up again.".

It has been revealed that the Russian invasion of Ukraine has led to NATO arming itself on a massive scale. Members have committed to raising their countries' defense spending to 5% of their gross domestic product (GDP) by 2035.

Rutte warned that all the allies needed a credible path to get there, "and ideally, they get there sooner than 2035." In addition, he said weapons production among member states needed to further increase because "right now, demand still far exceeds the supply.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that the contribution by Germany's Bundeswehr armed forces to NATO was explained by Carsten Breuer, Germany's highest-ranking soldier. For example, the massive increase in military spending: "Our defense budget has tripled since 2021. The goal is to achieve the 5% target, which was set at the summit in The Hague, well before 2035." In the coming year, Germany's defense budget has risen to more than €139 billion ($151 billion).

The Bundeswehr was further developing into a "constantly modernized, effective and innovative army, Breuer mentioned. Also, a much larger one than before. "To reach our current capability goals we are expanding the Bundeswehr to a total of 460,000 soldiers by the mid-2030s," the German chief of defense said. Of those, 200,000 are to be reservists. "This is like walking a tightrope because we must find the right balance between growth and operational readiness.".

Following his speech, Breuer answered questions from the delegates who showed keen interest in the developments. The discussion was a preview of Breuer's newly introduced post: He has been voted in as the new chair of the NATO Military Committee and will move to the alliance's headquarters in Brussels mid-next year. Then he will become the principal military advisor to NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte. "I take this election as a sign of recognition that Germany has now accepted its responsibility as well as its role in security policy," Breuer remarked.

💡 Key Takeaways
