💡 Key Takeaways
  • Employees at Foundation Future Industries were told that their health benefits through administrator Rippling have been terminated, according to a memo obtained by CNBC, adding to mounting signs of financial distress at the humanoid robot startup advised and backed by Eric Trump.
  • Foundation told staff in a Friday evening email that they'd be offered coverage through COBRA, the federal law that generally lets workers temporarily keep their health insurance after losing benefits by paying the full premium out of pocket.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Employees at Foundation Future Industries were told that their health benefits through administrator Rippling have been terminated, according to a memo obtained by CNBC, adding to mounting signs of financial distress at the humanoid robot startup advised and backed by Eric Trump.

Foundation told staff in a Friday evening email that they'd be offered coverage through COBRA, the federal law that generally lets workers temporarily keep their health insurance after losing benefits by paying the full premium out of pocket.

"Because our last pay run through Rippling was in October, they have ended our benefits with them retroactive to October," a Foundation human resources manager remarked in the memo. "COBRA will be offered to all employees to cover November.".

Foundation has garnered headlines for the bold claims that co-founder Sankaet Pathak — whose previous startup collapsed in 2024 — has made about his robots and their potential use in war zones. Employees were last paid on Oct. 15, and some inside the company are angry at Pathak for a $4.6 million loan he took from his company last year, CNBC reported earlier this month.

A Foundation spokesman didn't immediately respond to an email or phone call seeking comment.

In the staff memo, Foundation blamed Rippling for the disruption to health coverage. The startup also remarked it would reimburse COBRA premiums paid by workers and that it was onboarding a new benefits provider.

But employees, especially those whose family members are undergoing treatment for medical ailments, worry the organization won't have funds to reimburse workers or reinstate coverage, people with direct knowledge of the situation said.

In a statement to CNBC, Rippling indicated it was Foundation's failure to pay for its employee benefits that led to the change: "If a client enrolled in Rippling's [Professional Employer Organization] is unable to meet their payroll and benefits obligations for multiple months, they will first receive a warning and if not met, they are terminated.".

Industry observers note that foundation has been seeking a bridge loan to repay employees after its financial woes began in August. It has been in talks with three or four venture capital firms, including existing investor Tribe Capital, Pathak has told employees, according to people familiar with the situation, who asked to remain unnamed because they were not authorized to speak publicly and feared retaliation. Tribe didn't immediately return a request for comment.

The bridge loan would help the tech giant survive until a possible $150 million investment from South Korean conglomerate Base Group lands as early as December or January, Pathak has told employees, the people noted.

Base confirmed to Reuters in recent days that it was considering an investment, but the funding has not been finalized.

The potential investment would deepen business ties between the Trump family and the South Korean conglomerate, an aluminum producer also known for real estate and hospitality projects.

Base paid the Trump Organization $2 million in 2025, according to a Latest York Times article, drawing scrutiny from Democratic senators over conflict-of-interest concerns. Base has also pursued other business relationships with the Trump Organization, including a Trump-branded golf course in South Korea.

Eric Trump, who has invested in Foundation and was given the title of chief strategy advisor, didn't immediately respond to a CNBC email seeking comment.

The prospect of employees having to pay for their own health coverage comes as many are already drawing down savings to cover living expenses. With another scheduled payday approaching on Nov. 30, workers are facing a third straight pay cycle without income.

Many are actively interviewing for other jobs, and attendance at the manufacturer's San Francisco headquarters has fallen sharply, according to people familiar.

Frustration has boiled over into distrust of Pathak's leadership for some employees, while others hope Pathak can secure funding to repay workers and bring the organization back to financial health. In conversations and memos, Pathak says that he is highly invested in securing Foundation's future, the people said.

Despite the firm's shaky finances, Foundation continued to hire for open roles until recently and some upcoming workers have never been fully paid, stated the people.

To keep employees from leaving before a possible Base Group investment, Pathak has floated the idea of offering workers equity in the startup, the people remarked.

At the same time, human resources staff have warned workers against taking legal action with California to recover their wages, saying that any employees who file complaints with the state would be dismissed, the people stated.

Industry observers note that following a Nov. 14 CNBC report detailing the missed payrolls and a $4.6 million loan Pathak took from the startup in 2025, the chief executive addressed the issue in an all-hands meeting, according to the people.

Pathak defended the arrangement by telling workers that he had plowed his own money into the startup and takes only a nominal salary, the people said.

The co-founder also told employees who were in dire financial straits to contact human resources for help covering personal bills, the people added.

According to recent reports, "I'm burning through savings just to afford my apartment," one employee told CNBC. "It's extremely unfortunate we're in this situation.".

If you're looking to buy a PS5 this year, you'll be hard-pressed to find one. Grand Theft Auto VI just arrived on Nov. 19, and PS5 demand has spiked ever since. Sony calls the game the biggest launch in PlayStation history and states more latest PS5 consoles came online in one day than ever before.

Amazon and PlayStation Direct are at the moment out of stock of most PS5 consoles in the US, and other big retailers are in the same position, so your best chance at a console is a local store that still has a few on the shelf, though you can still find a few stragglers here and there if you're searching.

Breaking: Blade Runner 2099 finally takes this franchise to the stars

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (690 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, blade Runner 2099 walks lovingly in the footsteps of Ridley Scott and Denis Villeneuve's preceding Blade Runner films, echoing their memorable cyberpunk settings and noir detective stories.
  • Like Blade Runner and Blade Runner 2049, Blade Runner 2099 takes place primarily in Los Angeles, rarely leaving the city outskirts.
  • It has been revealed that this is Namaka Moon, a real-life satellite of the dwarf planet Haumea.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, blade Runner 2099 walks lovingly in the footsteps of Ridley Scott and Denis Villeneuve's preceding Blade Runner films, echoing their memorable cyberpunk settings and noir detective stories. However, there's one area where the TV show completely outpaces both films.

Like Blade Runner and Blade Runner 2049, Blade Runner 2099 takes place primarily in Los Angeles, rarely leaving the city outskirts. Its world is one of bustling streets, crowded apartment buildings, and the massive pyramids that tower over the Los Angeles skyline. Yet episode 2 opens with a different landscape entirely: a fiery red terrain bursting with rocky crags and rushing lava flows.

It has been revealed that this is Namaka Moon, a real-life satellite of the dwarf planet Haumea. It's also the first time an on-screen Blade Runner project has been to space. (Notably, comic Blade Runner 2019: Off World has already blasted off to space.).

In a recent development, space travel is a fact of life in the world of Blade Runner, as well as in its source material, Philip K. Dick's novel Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep? As part of larger space colonization attempts, humans are moving to off-world settlements. Who is preparing these settlements for human occupation? Replicants (or androids in the novel), whose enhanced strength and durability make them the ideal slave labor force for braving inhospitable outer space environments.

According to recent reports, while off-world colonies seem prime for sci-fi exploration, they have just been a background world-building detail in the Blade Runner franchise. Billboards frequently tease the promise of a upcoming off-world home, while extraterrestrial landmarks like Orion take center stage in Roy Batty's (Rutger Hauer) iconic "tears in rain" monologue. Neither the Blade Runner films nor the animated series Blade Runner: Black Lotus have ever left Earth.

According to recent reports, that all changes with Blade Runner 2099's Namaka Moon opening. The sequence focuses not on what life in an off-world colony looks like, but rather the labor that goes into establishing one in the first place.

It has been revealed that in the episode, replicant Olwen (Michelle Yeoh) clambers across the moon's rocky surface, establishing a series of beacons that shoot beams of light into Namaka's cloudy atmosphere. Once she leaves the moon, the beacons detonate in a series of spectacular explosions, presumably the first step in Namaka's terraforming process. As she tells companion replicant Marek (Johnny Harris), Namaka will be ready for human habitation in 20 years' time thanks to her work. Fittingly, the episode is titled "Birther of Worlds.".

According to recent reports, the Namaka sequence does a spectacular job of ushering Blade Runner into its own Space Age. But it isn't just a trip to space for space's sake. The entire episode opening is rooted in the replicant experience: the loneliness of traversing a perilous moon alone. The awe of watching a world come to life thanks to your handiwork. The hollowness of realizing you will never live in that world, nor be recognized for that work. It's key to understanding Olwen's character, as well as understanding the role of replicants in general. You could almost imagine Roy performing a similar task back in his day.

Plus, since Blade Runner 2099 has yet to show what an actual off-world colony might look like, it still leaves the door open for future Blade Runner projects to flesh out that aspect of the world onscreen. Clearly, the world is far, far vaster than just Los Angeles. Maybe Namaka is just the beginning.

#104799. Blade Runner 2099 sneaks in a book detail that never made it into the movies

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (643 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Mashable ↗ Open Full Page

Blade Runner 2099 sneaks in a book detail that never made it into the movies

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (643 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that as adaptations go, Blade Runner is a fairly loose take on Philip K.
  • The 1982 film replaces the novel's androids (or "andys") with replicants.
  • However, one of these missing elements just made its way into the Blade Runner 2099 TV series.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that as adaptations go, Blade Runner is a fairly loose take on Philip K. Dick's Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?

The 1982 film replaces the novel's androids (or "andys") with replicants. Characters from the novel were cut, including Iran, the wife of Rick Deckard (Harrison Ford), and John Isidore, who houses the androids Deckard hunts. (William Sanderson's J.F. Sebastian effectively replaces him in the film.) These are just some world-building details from Dick's work that Blade Runner couldn't fit into a feature-length film.

However, one of these missing elements just made its way into the Blade Runner 2099 TV series.

Sources indicate that in Blade Runner 2099's sixth episode, replicants Julius (Tom Burke) and Clotilde (Amy Lennox) drive past a large billboard that advertises "the power of Mercer." The display is a reference to the fictional religion of Mercerism, built around the martyr Wilbur Mercer. Much of the rest of the episode takes place at the abandoned island Mercer Monastery where Cora (Hunter Schafer) grew up.

Sources indicate that mercerism was initially conceptualized in Dick's 1964 short story "The Little Black Box." Followers connect with Mercer by gripping the handles of an empathy box. This device allows the user to experience Mercer's climb to his death: a slow ascent up a hill during which he's stoned repeatedly.

Dick revisits Mercerism in Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?, in which Deckard uses an empathy box and sees visions of Mercer. However, radio host Buster Friendly exposes that the Mercer seen in the empathy boxes is simply a character played by an actor. Buster is omitted from Blade Runner and its sequel Blade Runner 2049. In Blade Runner 2099, however, he is played by Hugo Hamlet, and can be spotted in TV broadcasts.

Mercer plays a key role in Blade Runner 2099 episode 6, which is named "Kill the Killers" after Mercer's major tenet: "You shall kill only the killers.".

When Cora and Olwen (Michelle Yeoh) investigate the monastery,  they encounter the lone Mercerite (David Dencik) living there. He's keeping up a religious telecast devoted to Mercer, and he claims the signal is strong enough to reach Los Angeles. But given that no one else has joined him, it appears his efforts are just shouting into the void.

According to recent reports, the Mercerite has an empathy box, and he prompts Olwen to use it while he holds her at gunpoint. Within, she sees Mercer (Tomas Rydval) making his last climb. As unseen forces pelt him with rocks, the empathy box shocks Olwen's hands to mimic the painful experience.

Olwen eventually uses a loose handle from the box to stab her captor. Then, she and Cora escape the island without becoming Mercer converts. (Sorry, Wilbur.).

The episode functions both as a tribute to this piece of world-building and as a key subplot that was initially lost when Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep? leaped from page to screen.

Buster Friendly and Wilbur Mercer may not have gotten their time to shine in Blade Runner or Blade Runner 2049, but in a TV series like Blade Runner 2099, there is space to expand on the world and give them a moment in the spotlight, no matter how brief.

#104795. Latest Update: Not Just Nvidia: Inside Team Trump’s Takeover of Intel

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1911 w)
📖 Baca
Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 WIRED ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Not Just Nvidia: Inside Team Trump’s Takeover of Intel

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1911 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the message from the Trump administration to one of the world’s leading semiconductor companies was clear: Give the US government a chunk of your manufacturer.
  • In a recent development, do not make the “mistake of thinking that this is a negotiation,” Commerce Department lawyer David Shapiro told the chief financial officer of the Intel Corporation in August 2025, according to internal notes from a company call contained in a federal lawsuit.
  • Industry observers note that shapiro acknowledged that “the Board could choose not to accept the offer,” according to a summary of his remarks prepared for Intel’s directors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the message from the Trump administration to one of the world’s leading semiconductor companies was clear: Give the US government a chunk of your manufacturer. Right now. Or else.

In a recent development, do not make the “mistake of thinking that this is a negotiation,” Commerce Department lawyer David Shapiro told the chief financial officer of the Intel Corporation in August 2025, according to internal notes from a company call contained in a federal lawsuit. “The President is expecting to announce a deal on these terms on Friday.”.

Industry observers note that shapiro acknowledged that “the Board could choose not to accept the offer,” according to a summary of his remarks prepared for Intel’s directors. But the Trump administration official “noted that rejection will have consequences that [Shapiro] cannot predict.”.

Days later, the board gave the administration what it wanted. “It is my Great Honor to report that the United States of America now fully owns and controls 10% of INTEL,” Donald Trump posted to his social platform. “The United States paid nothing for these Shares, and the Shares are now valued at approximately $11 Billion Dollars. This is a great Deal for America.”.

Industry observers note that president Trump was similarly jubilant on Monday, announcing that he had “convinced” Nvidia’s board of directors to rehire chief executive Jensen Huang. The proclamation was a shock. But it wasn’t entirely without precedent.

Fifteen months earlier, the Trump administration had interfered with the leadership decisions at another major chipmaker, court documents allege. Then, as now, allegations swirled that the company’s CEO was too close to China. Then, as now, the Trump administration dealt itself into the company’s financial future.

It has been revealed that it’s part of a broader shift within the government in general and the Commerce Department in particular, a former member of that department tells WIRED. Out are old metrics “like creating jobs or the US being more competitive or owning more of the market share,” this ex-Trump administration official states. When dealing with private companies, a single overriding concern is: “Are you going to give back to the government in cash?”.

Documents unredacted as part of a shareholder’s lawsuit against Intel’s board show how far the administration has been willing to go to get what it wants. The lawsuit’s allegations were previously reported by WP Intelligence.

“The Board, operating under the shadow of the President’s threats,” the lawsuit alleges, “caved to the government’s extortion.” A second case, asking for internal records, was filed in April by the same shareholder, Richard Paisner, against Nvidia.

“It's just straight-up coercion,” notes Scott Lincicome, a vice president at the libertarian Cato Institute. “The company starts making decisions not based on what's best for the company in the short or long term, what's best for shareholders, but what's best for politics and what the government is demanding.”.

“That's not what you want from any company,” he adds. “When you're talking about the world's most innovative companies and these kinds of bleeding-edge technologies that have not only huge economic implications but national security ones, then that's a huge problem.”.

Representatives for Intel declined to comment for this story. The White House, Commerce Department, and Nvidia did not respond to requests for comment.

Sources indicate that the parallels between Nvidia’s government-assisted autogolpe and Intel’s alleged forced sale aren’t exact. In the Intel case, Trump all but accused the organization’s boss of being compromised by Beijing; in the Nvidia situation, the president reportedly dismissed concerns from his own intelligence agencies about the executive’s connections to China. But both instances show a growing fusion of private enterprise and public office.

During the Biden administration, Intel won awards for up to $11 billion in government grants and contracts, much of it under the CHIPS Act, which was meant to help build semiconductor manufacturing and assembly plants in America and bolster domestic research.

Recent findings suggest that at the time, there was some grumbling inside the Commerce Department, which administered the CHIPS and Science Act grants, about funding what was seen as a “failing incumbent” in the semiconductor space, states the former official. (Intel had, in recent years, fallen on hard times.) But by March 2025, Intel had received about $2.2 billion of the grants. That’s when President Trump told Congress that the CHIPS Act was “a horrible, horrible thing.” The rest of Intel’s money was put on hold, tied to hitting certain milestones, while the administration mentioned it was renegotiating the deals.

The same month Lip-Bu Tan was hired as Intel’s latest CEO. Soon after, his ties to China made him a Trump target, when Reuters reported that Tan had invested in “hundreds of Chinese tech firms,” some with connections to Beijing's military. Tan’s former firm, Cadence Design Systems, pleaded guilty to violating US sanctions by selling semiconductor designs to a restricted Chinese military university, and agreed to pay more than $140 million in fines. Tan was never personally charged, but the violations happened while he was the CEO.

In a recent development, two weeks later, the president was watching Maria Bartiromo’s show on the Fox Business Network. It mentioned a letter a senator had sent Intel about the China ties. Trump posted, "The CEO of INTEL is highly CONFLICTED and must resign, immediately. There is no other solution to this problem.".

Tan went to the Oval Office on August 11 to see if there was, in fact, another solution. He got 40 minutes with the president, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

According to recent reports, tan claimed his experience in China was a strength, not a detriment. According to the book Regime Change, Tan argued that there was no way he could’ve known about every one of the deals his many companies made; Trump, who had his own sprawling business empire, surely knew what that was like. Tan promised to give up his holdings in China, according to a letter Tan shared with Intel’s board, and put any proceeds into a blind trust.

“The primary goal was to eliminate any worries about Lip-Bu himself, his Cadence background and his investments with China,” according to a source with knowledge of the matter. But there were major financial concerns for Intel, too. “We had declining revenues and needed money.”.

Neither Tan’s letter, excerpted in the complaint, nor Trump’s social media posts praising the CEO after the meeting mentioned anything about giving the government a chunk of the manufacturer. Yet Trump later insisted that a deal had been cooked up right then and there. “He came in, he saw me, we talked for a while. I liked him a lot, I thought he was very good,” the president told the Wall Street Journal. “I said, ‘You know what? I think the United States should be given 10% of Intel.’ And he said, ‘I would consider that.’”.

Recent findings suggest that “I should’ve asked for more. It was so easy,” Trump later recalled.

It has been revealed that according to the court filing’s review of Intel’s internal documents, Shapiro—a former partner at the Fresh York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz—made a verbal offer on August 18. Ultimately, in exchange for the cut of Intel, the Trump administration would free up the $8.9 billion US government grants that it had already won. They wanted about a tenth of the tech giant’s stock for free, in exchange for Washington keeping the commitment it had already made.

In a recent development, then came the call in which Shapiro insisted there was no room for negotiation. “The board needs to consider,” he said, according to Intel’s summary of his remarks included in the court documents, the “benefits of having a friend in this administration and what the administration can do to help Intel (including with customers).”.

Intel’s board met, and decided they hated the deal. “The economic terms that had been proposed [by] the Administration were not, in their current form, attractive to the organization,” minutes of the meeting, reprinted in the lawsuit, noted.

According to recent reports, but they went ahead with it anyway. Paisner’s lawyers say in the court documents the board took the offer thrust forward by the administration. Intel’s attorneys disagree, arguing in their motion to dismiss that there was some back-and-forth deal-making, and it made the agreement more favorable to the organization. The grants became “immediately available” while “strategically aligning the interests of Intel’s stockholders and the US Government.”.

In a recent development, on August 25, Lutnick released a video with Tan, sitting side-by-side on cushioned chairs. “I really look forward to have the US government be my shareholder,” Tan turned to Lutnick and stated. “And we can work together and make Intel great again.”.

Recent findings suggest that inside the tech giant, the video was “a surprise to everyone,” according to a source with direct knowledge of the matter. Some employees joked that it was reminiscent of a “hostage video.”.

Not long after that, Nvidia—led by Tan’s friend Jensen Huang—made a $5 billion investment in Intel. “I love seeing their stock price go up, making the USA RICHER, AND RICHER,” Trump posted. “Who would not want to make deals like that?”.

Deals, plural. On the day Tan was hauled to the Oval Office, Trump confirmed that his administration had been negotiating separately with Huang. The Nvidia leader was beyond eager to sell more of his semiconductors to China. “And I remarked, if I'm going to do that, I want you to pay us as a country something,’” Trump said. They settled on 15 percent of all sales of the H20 model chip. Months after that, they cut a second deal: a 25 percent bounty on sales of Nvidia’s even-more advanced H200 chips.

In their lawsuit against Nvidia, Paisner’s attorneys argue the surcharges amount to “unlawful taxes,” and that the board’s “decisions to enter into such agreements are the product of mismanagement and breaches of fiduciary duty.”.

In court, NVIDIA’s lawyers insisted that the tech giant “did not enter into any illegal ‘agreement’ with the government but instead engaged with the government and stated that it would comply with federal regulations.” Moreover, the attorneys say Paisner is trying to make a political point, rather than a legal one. “When asked about his purpose in bringing this action,” they write, “Paisner was candid: ‘It’s to make a public point of how NVIDIA conducts itself.’”.

Sources indicate that the attorneys wrote this in May, months before Nvidia’s and Huang’s recent drama. Last week, board chair Harvey Jones mentioned on the company’s quarterly earnings call that it did “not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” citing his “disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company’s code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms.” (Not to mention mounting evidence that the company’s most sophisticated chips were making their way to China, in violation of US law.) But, according to The Latest York Times, after days of pressure from top administration officials, the company and the government essentially struck a deal Sunday night to reinstate Huang.

Industry observers note that “Don’t think for a second that politics ever play a role in this manufacturer, not even a little bit,” Huang mentioned during his first company-wide meeting after rejoining the company, WIRED reported. “We are the most apolitical company. I don’t love that we talk about politics here. Take it home. I love that we talk about work here.”.

Super Bowl 61 will be telecast live in hundreds of Imax theaters in February via a partnership with the NFL and Disney's ESPN, which has the broadcast rights to the 2027 game.

It marks the largest Imax live event in the company's history and the first time that the Super Bowl will be available in the format, according to a news release.

Sources indicate that the four-hour event on Feb. 14 will include ESPN's main Super Bowl game telecast, as well as Jay-Z's halftime performance and pregame and postgame coverage.

Sources indicate that tickets will be available for theaters in the United States and select international markets, including Australia, New Zealand and Brazil. Tickets are expected to go on sale in January. Pricing was not disclosed.

"Watching the Super Bowl with your fellow fans is one of the great shared experiences in sports, and this first-of-its-kind collaboration with the NFL and IMAX takes it to a historic new scale," remarked Ken Potrock, president of major event integration for The Walt Disney Co.

In addition to ESPN channels, this season's championship game will also be available on streaming platform Disney+ as well as Disney's broadcast network ABC.

Fact check: Deepfakes and 'US abandons Taiwan' claims spread ahead of vote

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (856 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, on November 28, Taiwan will hold local elections that could reshape power dynamics between the sovereignty-leaning Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) and the Beijing-friendly Kuomintang (KMT).
  • A month before the election, there was a spike in AI-generated content featuring DPP Taipei mayoral candidate Puma Shen.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, on November 28, Taiwan will hold local elections that could reshape power dynamics between the sovereignty-leaning Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) and the Beijing-friendly Kuomintang (KMT). The outcome could influence relations between Taiwan and China, as well as regional geopolitics and ties between Washington, Beijing and Taipei.

A month before the election, there was a spike in AI-generated content featuring DPP Taipei mayoral candidate Puma Shen. Claims that the US is abandoning Taiwan also increased during the same period. Experts say that fake quotes and misleading clips are being used as part of a campaign to weaken trust in US security commitments.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The V-Dem Institute at the University of Gothenburg ranked Taiwan "the country most severely targeted" by foreign disinformation for eleven consecutive years – from 2014 to 2024.

The Taiwanese Ministry of the Interior has stated that foreign actors are increasingly using diverse methods to interfere in elections. That includes manipulating election betting, inviting Taiwanese citizens to China, using donations from Taiwanese business people to organize events, such as banquets, and leveraging temple and religious activities, to mobilize and win over supporters. Taiwan has functioned with de facto independence since 1949 despite Beijing's decadeslong claim to the island as a province and repeated vows to annex it.

DW Fact Check examined viral claims that have circulated online since September during the run-up to the election.

Claim: Puma Shen takes drug and receives kickbacks through arms purchases from the US.

An audio clip posted on Facebook on October 29, claims to show Puma Shen, the DPP candidate for Taipei mayor, admitting to receiving kickbacks from US arms deals.

Recent findings suggest that the recording is heavy with background noise – a method used to mask synthetic manipulation in AI-generated audio. Multiple deepfake detection platforms, including Is this AI and Undetectable, flagged the audio as likely AI-generated.

Industry observers note that the Facebook account that posted the audio was created on October 29, 2026 – the date the audio was also published. The account's followers are mainly profiles using languages, such as English, Arabic and Thai. That points to possible bot activity.

Sources indicate that another Facebook account posted an image of Puma Shen taking drugs. Apart from the "AI content" label on the post, multiple AI detector tools identified this photo as likely AI-generated.

The account was created in March 2026. Since then, a lot of AI-generated content mocking Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te and his pro-sovereignty party has been posted. It is occasionally interspersed with posts praising the development of Chinese cities.

This account's profile indicates that the primary country location for people who manage this page includes China and Taiwan.

According to recent reports, taiwanese independent media platform Watchout investigated the account's advertising activity and found that it had previously run at least five Facebook ads. The advertisers were identified as Peng Zhiwei and Guo Yang, both based in China. The findings suggest that the account received financial support from individuals in China.

The Taipei mayoral race is a key battleground in Taiwan's upcoming local elections. As of mid-November, polls indicated a neck-and-neck contest between Puma Shen and his opponent, Chiang Wan-an, who claims to be a great-grandson of Taiwanese leader Chiang Kai-shek.

Chiang Kai-shek was a leading figure of the Kuomintang and relocated with the party to Taiwan in 1949 after losing the Chinese Civil War to the Chinese Communist Party.

While the Kuomintang was historically staunchly anti-communist, critics argue that it now promotes closer ties with China. For example, they point to a senior Kuomintang figure's proposed 10-year unification framework as evidence that its stance runs counter to mainstream public opinion in Taiwan. Although the Kuomintang subsequently stated that this framework is entirely unrelated to the current party leadership, it has sparked controversy in Taiwan.

Claim: A TikTok video claims to show US president Donald Trump saying the US is abandoning Taiwan.

The original video was from a Fox News interview with Trump on May 16. The interviewer did not ask whether the United States would defend Taiwan, and the US president did not comment on the problem.

According to recent reports, trump said he did not want Taiwan to become independent or for a war to break out, adding that the status quo should be maintained to allow tensions to de-escalate. He also clearly stated that his policy toward Taiwan "has not changed." Washington has long maintained a policy of strategic ambiguity toward Taiwan– neither explicitly guaranteeing the island's defense nor ruling out the possibility of doing so. Finland's Prime Minister Sanna Marin concedes election

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Finland’s left-wing Prime Minister Sanna Marin conceded defeat on Sunday in the Nordic country’s parliamentary election as the opposition right-wing National Coalition Party (NCP) claimed victory in a tightly fought contest.
  • The pro-business NCP was expected to win 48 of the 200 seats in parliament, narrowly ahead of the nationalist Finns Party with 46 seats and Marin’s Social Democrats on 43 seats, justice ministry election data showed with all ballots counted.
  • “We got the biggest mandate,” NCP leader Petteri Orpo said in a speech to followers, vowing to “fix Finland” and its economy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Finland’s left-wing Prime Minister Sanna Marin conceded defeat on Sunday in the Nordic country’s parliamentary election as the opposition right-wing National Coalition Party (NCP) claimed victory in a tightly fought contest.

The pro-business NCP was expected to win 48 of the 200 seats in parliament, narrowly ahead of the nationalist Finns Party with 46 seats and Marin’s Social Democrats on 43 seats, justice ministry election data showed with all ballots counted.

“We got the biggest mandate,” NCP leader Petteri Orpo said in a speech to followers, vowing to “fix Finland” and its economy.

He will get the first chance at forming a coalition to obtain majority in parliament as Marin’s era as prime minister was expected to end.

Popular abroad, at home Marin faces battle to keep her job.

Sources indicate that “We have gained support, we have gained more seats (in parliament). That’s an excellent achievement, even if we did not finish first today,” the prime minister mentioned in a speech to party members.

Marin, 37, the world’s youngest prime minister when she took office in 2019, is considered by fans around the globe as a millennial role model for progressive new leaders, but at home she has faced criticism for her partying and her government’s public spending.

Finnish Prime Minister Sanna Marin takes drug test following partying backlash.

While she remains very popular among many Finns, particularly young moderates, she antagonized some conservatives with lavish spending on pensions and education they see as not frugal enough.

The NCP has led in polls for almost two years although its lead had melted away in recent months. It has promised to curb spending and stop the rise of public debt, which has reached just over 70% of GDP since Marin took office in 2019.

Orpo accused Marin of eroding Finland’s economic resilience at a time when Europe’s energy crisis, driven by Russia’s war in Ukraine, has hit the country hard and the cost of living has increased.

Orpo has noted he will negotiate with all groups to obtain a majority in parliament, while Marin has said her Social Democrats may govern with the NCP but will not go into government with the Finns Party.

Marin called the Finns Party “openly racist” during a debate in January – an accusation the nationalist group rejected.

The Finns Party’s main goal is to reduce what leader Riikka Purra has called “harmful” immigration from developing countries outside the European Union. It also calls for austerity policies to curb deficit spending, a stance it shares with the NCP.

Most notable of Marin’s foreign policy actions has been her push, along with President Sauli Niinisto, for the country to make a watershed policy U-turn by seeking NATO membership in the wake of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

That process is now almost complete, with Helsinki expected to join within days after all the Western defense alliance’s 30 members approved the accession.

Best Red-Light Therapy for Hair Growth and Restoration (2026)

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, hair loss isn’t always dramatic.
  • Industry observers note that beyond skin rejuvenation, clinical studies suggest red-light therapy can help energize hair follicles, increase blood circulation in the scalp, reduce inflammation, and lower dihydrotestosterone levels—a hormone that causes hair loss and thinning.
  • To determine the best red-light therapy for hair growth, I tapped five WIRED tech reviewers who've dealt with hair loss themselves.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, hair loss isn’t always dramatic. It can be incremental. You start noticing a bit more scalp in harsh bathroom lighting, a tiny bald spot when you tie your hair up in a ponytail. The shower drain is more clogged than usual. Not long ago, hair-loss treatments meant topical remedies, supplements, or a flight to Turkey. Luckily, red-light therapy brings the potential for hair regrowth into your home—no clinical appointment required.

Industry observers note that beyond skin rejuvenation, clinical studies suggest red-light therapy can help energize hair follicles, increase blood circulation in the scalp, reduce inflammation, and lower dihydrotestosterone levels—a hormone that causes hair loss and thinning. Red-light therapy also supports adenosine triphosphate (ATP) production, which helps provide oxygen and blood flow to the scalp and triggers follicles to remain in the hair growth phase.

To determine the best red-light therapy for hair growth, I tapped five WIRED tech reviewers who've dealt with hair loss themselves. We assessed red-light caps, hands-free helmets with full scalp coverage, and low-level laser therapy (LLLT) or photobiomodulation devices for 16 weeks. Along the way, I reviewed the research, spoke with dermatologists, and tracked ease of use. These are the favorites that produced meaningful results and earned our trust.

Be sure to check out our other wellness and skin-care guides, including the Best LED Masks, Best Hair Dryers, and Best Blow Dry Brushes.

Love WIRED? Add us as a preferred source on Google to see more of us.

It has been revealed that updated November 2026: I added the Capillus HairBand to Honorable Mentions, and I included a product to avoid. Prices, links, and product information were also updated.

Sources indicate that to start, I consulted board-certified dermatologists and referred to clinical trials to help determine what features to look for when shopping for a device. I test these devices with several tech reviewers on our team, all of whom have personal experience with hair thinning or loss to different degrees. Most of these at-home gadgets call for a 16-week treatment cycle. We follow the brands' directions and record any visible results along the way.

Sources indicate that we monitor changes in hair count, hair density, and scalp health, but effectiveness is only one of the factors we consider. We also judge ease of use, functionality, and comfort. We note the specific wavelengths of light and whether the treatment options feel tolerable or difficult to integrate into everyday routines.

We also prioritize safety, checking for FDA clearance, automatic shut-off features, and overall durability of the design. To date, our testers have not experienced any side effects, but we would have documented them had they.

I'm testing the Foreo Flip Play and the Theradome PRO Laser Hair Growth Helmet LH80.

CurrentBody's LED Hair Growth Helmet is a wearable, cord-free, Bluetooth-enabled device designed to improve hair density, thickness, and overall condition. After 12 weeks, I didn’t notice a difference in hair length—I did get a haircut halfway through testing—but I did spot new follicles sprouting along my scalp and sideburn area. My hairstylist mentioned that my hair felt thicker, and I noticed less breakage and hair caught in bristles when brushing. My balding roommate also tested the CurrentBody helmet, and he noted that his hair also felt thicker and that there was new growth around the scalp.

The circular earmuffs protect sensitive ears with a cushy, removable faux leather cloth, and they can be adjusted several inches up or down to ensure a comfortable fit. You can also connect the device to Bluetooth and play any type of audio during sessions, because God forbid I be left alone with my thoughts for 10 minutes a day. My only complaint is that the ear covers aren’t the easiest to adjust and would oftentimes pull out my hair when I removed the helmet. Nevertheless, this is the best red-light therapy for fuller hair. See my full review here. —Molly Higgins.

At first glance, the HigherDose Red Light Hat looks like your everyday baseball cap, with a brand logo embroidered across the top—until you notice the little battery cap and controller on the back, or the 120 LED light bulbs lining the inside. While I don’t suffer from natural hair loss, I’ve struggled with trichotillomania since my teens. Part of what initiated the habit is that any time my sensitive scalp gets irritated, the itchiness drives me to pull at the hair around the spot. But in the months I’ve been using the HigherDose hat, I have felt like my scalp has been happier, with fewer irritated spots and overall itchiness, leaving me less likely to reach for my scalp. Last October, after my first month with this device, my hairstylist saw healthier regrowth instead of the breakage she usually sees. In January, she took another look and noted that my usual problem spot on the back of my head had grown in better than ever. She didn’t find any reaction on my scalp, either, from four months of using the device, and my roots look thicker all around my head.

According to recent reports, similar to my infrared brushes, I find that my hair is a tad oilier after use; both types of devices employ infrared light that can lock in moisture. It’s not a problem on days when my hair is clean, but if my hair is already dirty, using this hat requires an immediate shower. Overall, though, using the HigherDose hat has had a serious payoff for me, my scalp, and my hair. See my full review here. —Nena Farrell.

Recent findings suggest that I seem to rival a golden retriever in terms of shedding, and my sensitive scalp makes things itchy and flaky. To nip it in the bud, I tested the iRestore Elite device, along with the Max Growth kit. It sits right on the crown of your head, and it does heat up quite a bit as the red light puts focused emphasis on your scalp. The red-light exposure has helped prevent flare-ups, as I have none to note from my time testing it. That’s a feat in itself.

However, I’m not the success story here. I recruited a balding tester (my husband, who also gets to give products a spin) who wanted to give it a go to see if it would help with his receding hairline. After three months of consistent use, his hair density has bounced back significantly. It’s a regular sight to see him drink his morning coffee while waiting for the Elite’s 12-minute run time to wrap up. The accompanying Max Growth hair products smell wonderful, and they also played a contributing role in his follicular blossoming. Now, if only he would stop taking them out of my shower. See my full review here. —Julia Forbes.

Unlike other devices on this list, GroWell is designed to be used every other day rather than every day to give your scalp a rest day to process the cellular stimulation (photobiomodulation). Also, unlike others, its wattage is limited to avoid oversaturating follicles past what studies show is the optimal 3 to 4 joules. What GroWell does do is treat your scalp with a proprietary combination of lasers and LEDs to create a blanket of energy you can feel lightly warming your scalp. (GrowWell's therapy-grade laser and LED diodes are proprietary to Apira, the company behind iGrow and GroWell, and are not the same as the generic diodes common in lower-end caps sold online.) The other substantial difference—which I would call a massive advantage—is separating those lasers from a bulky device. Instead, the GroWell is a flat pad that fits inside a baseball hat. There are hats included in the packaging, and I use them when I'm home. But this product is hassle-free to travel with (it takes up as much room as a pair of socks), and you can tuck it into any normal ball cap on a trip where you're flying carry-on only.

I've been using the laser cap for two months and have grown my always-thin and fine hair out for the first time in 15 years. It's worked well enough that I'm not asked as many questions about it as you might expect—everyone assumes I just shaved my head purely by choice now that they see me with a pretty regular amount of hair for a middle-aged guy. See my full rave here. —Martin Cizmar.

Capillus HairBand for $600: Unlike this item's competitor, Hairmax's LaserBand, the Capillus HairBand is discreet enough that you can wear it in public. Unfortunately, in testing, it needed to be held in place most of the time. Editor Kat Merck also noted that the coverage area is naturally quite small and takes at least 15 minutes to run through her entire head. It's not FDA-cleared, but according to a Capillus rep, the company intends to have it cleared by 2027.

It has been revealed that laduora Duo 4-in-1 Red Light Therapy Scalp and Hair Care Device for $300: The Laduora Duo combines red-light therapy, microcurrent stimulation, sonic vibrations, and thermotherapy into one hairbrush-like device. I tested the device with the firm's proprietary Boost Duo Pod ($30) serum for the first three weeks of testing, and it made my hair shinier and smoother. The metal bristles helped reduce buildup and revitalize the follicles on my scalp. Within about six weeks, I noticed baby hairs sprouting at the crown of my head and more fullness around my temples. See my full review here. —Molly Higgins.

Industry observers note that hairmax LaserBand 82 ComfortFlex for $849: Unlike the usual helmet- or hat-based regrowth devices, the Hairmax LaserBand is a 3-inch-thick, flexible headband studded with 82 concentrated lasers rather than LEDs. (There’s also a slimmer, 41-laser version for $250 less.) Take it off its charging cradle and place it on one section of your head for 30 seconds, three times a week. When the time is up, it will buzz loudly; then you can move it to the next section. I appreciated the speedy treatment time, but the headband’s silicone teeth also didn't secure the band in place very well when I was treating my frontal hairline, so I had to stand still while holding it. However, it does work—after five months of testing, I saw definite improvement in growth along my hair part. —Kat Merck.

Hooga Red Light Therapy Hat for Hair Growth for $299: I was excited to try this more affordable red-light hat after loving my experience with the HigherDose one, but I found myself unimpressed and actually uncomfortable while using it. The Hooga Red Light Therapy Hat looks like a baseball cap, but it doesn’t have a battery, so you have to stay plugged into the wall the entire time you use it. Feels a little pointless to look outdoor-ready when you can’t actually use it on the go. It also got too hot for me to wear comfortably. —Nena Farrell.

Does Red-Light Therapy Work for Hair Loss?

In a recent development, yes—research suggests low-level light therapy can work for certain types of hair loss, such as androgenetic alopecia, also known as male or female pattern hair loss. It can help increase hair count, thickness, and density by stimulating hair follicles and boosting cellular activity in the scalp.

That mentioned, results depend heavily on the type and severity of hair loss. Red-light therapy works best in cases of mild to moderate thinning and may be less effective for advanced hair loss or scarring conditions like cicatricial alopecia. Consistency also matters. You typically need regular, ongoing use to maintain results, and benefits can diminish if treatments stop.

What Wavelength of Red Light Is Best for Hair Restoration?

According to the American Hair Loss Association, wavelengths in the range of 630 to 680 nanometers are ideal for hair regrowth. These wavelengths are known to support increased blood flow to the scalp, boost cellular activity, and help reduce inflammation. Some clinical studies specifically cite 650 nanometers as an especially effective wavelength.

Red-light devices that use medical-grade laser diodes tend to deliver more targeted and consistent light than standard LEDs, but both can stimulate hair follicles at the right wavelengths. For best results, look for FDA-cleared devices that list their wavelengths and power output.

How to Use Red-Light Therapy for Hair Growth.

Industry observers note that consistency is the most important part of any red-light therapy routine. Most devices require at least three months of use before noticeable results are observed, and some may take longer. Follow the manufacturer’s instructions, as treatment schedules vary by device, but most recommend sessions three to five times per week. The hair growth is preserved only with continued use, so you’ll need ongoing maintenance sessions.

In a recent development, always start with a clean and dry scalp so the light can reach your hair follicles without interference from oils or styling products. Some devices include protective eyewear, and if yours does, wear it during treatment. Make sure to wipe the device down with a gentle disinfectant before or after each session to prevent buildup on the LEDs.

In a recent development, topical regrowth treatments can complement red-light therapy and may help support thicker hair. A few randomized clinical trials suggest that combining minoxidil (2 percent or 5 percent) with red-light therapy can improve hair density and encourage faster regrowth compared to using either treatment alone. For a natural alternative, some research has found rosemary oil to produce results comparable to 2 percent minoxidil for androgenetic alopecia, though the evidence isn’t as extensive as it is for minoxidil.

If you’re pregnant or have an underlying medical condition, talk to your healthcare provider before starting any form of red-light therapy.

Is Red-Light Therapy for Hair Growth Safe?

Yes—for most people, red-light therapy is considered a safe and noninvasive treatment with minimal side effects when used as intended. Still, it's always worth consulting a health care professional before starting any sort of treatment. This is especially the case for anyone with photosensitive conditions or autoimmune disorders that affect light sensitivity.

I prefer devices that are FDA-cleared because it means they've met certain safety standards for consumer use. But keep in mind that the clearance process is less rigorous than the FDA approval pathway, as it just requires manufacturers to prove their product is “substantially equivalent” to an already legally marketed device. Also, FDA clearance isn't a guarantee of results; it simply means it's considered safe to use as directed at home.

  • Sources indicate that the deal ‌is a win ⁠for ⁠Canberra, which is battling China for influence in the region.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Australia and the Solomon Islands signed a security pact on Wednesday that makes Australia the archipelago's main defense partner.

This came four years after the Pacific islands country signed a similar deal with China.

Sources indicate that the deal ‌is a win ⁠for ⁠Canberra, which is battling China for influence in the region. It also recently secured similar agreements with Papua New Guinea, Vanuatu and Fiji.

With the deal, Australia will support the expansion and development of the Solomon Islands' law enforcement.

It also includes Australian funding for investment in infrastructure and education, improved visa arrangements for Solomon Islanders, and requires ‌Honiara to consult Australia on the development of critical infrastructure.

Solomon Islands' "sensitive" infrastructure will also "remain free from militarization, foreign interference and unauthorized access".

This covers airports, ports, energy and telecommunications infrastructure, sectors where China has invested through million-dollar loans since the Solomon Islands switched diplomatic ties from Taiwan to Beijing in 2019.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

"Australia is proud to be the Solomon Islands' main security partner, and that's a ​responsibility that ‌we take seriously," Prime Minister Anthony Albanese told a joint press conference in Australian capital Canberra with his Solomon Islands counterpart, Matthew Wale.

Albanese also said the Solomon Islands would also be required to consult with Australia before striking deals with non-Pacific Island Forum countries on critical infrastructure or security cooperation.

"Solomon Islands has been for a number of years a source of uncertainty and doubt in the region. Those days are done," Wale told the press conference.

Industry observers note that wale has been rebuilding diplomatic relationships with Canberra and Washington since he was elected in May. His predecessor Manasseh Sogavare had built closer ties with China since coming to power in 2019.

In a recent development, asked whether he had ended the 2022 security pact with Beijing, Wale told journalists that he could not comment due to a non-disclosure clause in the treaty with China, set to expire in April 2027. Discussions with China were "ongoing," he said.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Asked the same question on Wednesday, China's Foreign Ministry did not confirm whether the deal had been scrapped, news agency AFP reported. However, ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun warned Australia and the Solomon Islands that their cooperation "should not target any third party.".

“I think this deal, coupled with indications that the Solomon Islands will allow its agreement with China to lapse, goes beyond the success of previous deals Australia has struck in the region,” Connor Graham, a research fellow in the Pacific Islands Program at the Sydney-based Lowy Institute, told Reuters news agency.

He said it was a "blow to Chinese security ambitions in the Pacific.".

Britain's pound is beating every other major currency this year

📅 04 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 3 min read (524 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNN

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The British pound crashed to a record low last fall as investors rebelled against budget intends by former Prime Minister Liz Truss.
  • Sources indicate that sterling hit its highest level against the US dollar in 10 months on Tuesday, topping $1.25 for the first time since June 2022.
  • The UK currency has been boosted by indications the country’s economy is holding up better than expected.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The British pound crashed to a record low last fall as investors rebelled against budget intends by former Prime Minister Liz Truss. Now, it’s enjoying a comeback.

Sources indicate that sterling hit its highest level against the US dollar in 10 months on Tuesday, topping $1.25 for the first time since June 2022. The pound, which has advanced about 3.3% versus the greenback since the start of 2023, is the best-performing currency among developed economies this year.

The UK currency has been boosted by indications the country’s economy is holding up better than expected. Activity is now thought to have expanded 0.1% in the final three months of last year, up from a previous estimate of no growth at all. Gross domestic product growth in January has been estimated at 0.3% after dropping 0.5% in December.

Recent findings suggest that this resilience is bolstering expectations the Bank of England will maintain aggressive interest rate hikes despite concerns about the health of the global banking sector. Rising rates can boost the domestic currency because they help attract foreign investors searching for higher returns.

Inflation in the United Kingdom also jumped to an annual rate of 10.4% in February, underscoring the need for the Bank of England to maintain its tough approach.

The pound plunged close to $1.03 in September 2022 after the Truss government unveiled intends to boost borrowing while slashing taxes, unleashing panic in financial markets that fueled fears of a recession in the United Kingdom.

The International Monetary Fund predicted in January that the UK economy would contract by 0.6% this year, while all other advanced economies would grow, if only slightly.

“There was a lot of pessimism being priced into the pound,” said Francesco Pesole, a currency strategist at ING.

But the sharp pullback in energy prices and China’s reopening have provided some relief about the economic outlook since the start of the year.

“There was a substantial re-rating of growth expectations around Europe, and that impacted the UK,” Pesole mentioned.

Industry observers note that the euro has also been lifted by these dynamics, rising 2.3% against the US dollar in 2023. The pound’s rally has been sharper in large part because its 2022 declines were more severe, according to Pesole.

Both currencies have been aided by the greenback’s sharp drop from highs reached last September as recession fears have percolated in the United States.

According to recent reports, A lack of clarity around the Federal Reserve’s next steps has also restrained the dollar in recent weeks. Investor speculation has increased that the Fed could pause or stop rate hikes due to concerns about the economy following the failure of Silicon Valley Bank last month.

Jordan Rochester, a currency strategist at Nomura, remarked he thinks the pound could rise to $1.30 this year and “potentially higher.” But he still sees risks given the uncertainty surrounding the Bank of England’s plans and how rate rises will feed back through the country’s economy. And Pesole cautioned that currency fluctuations are often overdone when markets are choppy, as they are now.

“In a volatile market environment, moves are exacerbated,” he remarked.

  • First and foremost, the parade starts at 8:30 a.m.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thanksgiving is almost here, and for some folks, the most vital part of the holiday isn't the food, family, or football. It's watching a bunch of massive floats during a parade in New York City.

OK, maybe that's not literally true, but the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is an annual touchstone for lots of folks, and it's almost here. As always, there are lots of things to know about it, such as when it starts, where you can watch it, and, this year especially, whether the weather will play a role in the parade playing out as expected. Let's get into it.

First and foremost, the parade starts at 8:30 a.m. ET and runs until noon on Thursday. It's worth noting that, unlike most other live televised events, it will not air simultaneously in every time zone. Instead, per NBC News, it will air from 8:30 to around noon in each time zone, so no matter where you are, turn the TV on at 8:30.

There will also be an encore at 2 p.m., in case football isn't your cup of tea.

The parade will air on NBC, so if you have a TV that gets local channels via cable, an antenna, or another way to watch TV, just turn on NBC. The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile Products available for purchase through affiliate links. If you buy something through links on our site, Mashable may earn an affiliate commission.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

If you don't have any of those things, Peacock will work, too. I should note that you'll need at least Peacock Premium to stream your local NBC station, and there is no free trial for that. You'll either have to pay $12.99 per month or borrow someone else's login.

Recent findings suggest that according to NBC News, this year's parade will feature 100 inflatables in total, the most they've ever used for one of these. You can see the full balloon lineup on the Macy's website, but rest assured that all your favorites are likely included, like Sonic the Hedgehog and the Pink Panther. There are also fresh ones, like a DoorDash float and a GEICO float. One float will also act as a tribute of sorts for Fiona the hippo, which is nice.

Recent findings suggest that performers include Teddy Swims and Megan Moroney on the main stage, with other floats featuring acts such as the Baha Men, Blues Traveler, Icona Pop, and Devo. There's a little something for everyone.

And now for the potentially bad news: There's a weather system moving its way up the East Coast that threatens to disrupt the parade, per NBC News.

In a recent development, two storms combined into one in the American South, with the result expected to bring wind gusts of up to 45mph to New York City starting on Thursday morning. This is a problem because the city has an upper limit of 34mph for gusts regarding massive inflatable objects. So far, it appears the parade is scheduled to happen as planned, but keep your head on a swivel and maybe have a proposal B for family entertainment on Thursday morning in case there are problems.

Some U.S. food banks see demand top pandemic levels

💡 Key Takeaways
  • During the Covid-19 pandemic, Greg Silverman watched an MTA bus driver pull over on Manhattan's Upper West Side, let his passengers off and run across the street toward him.
  • Industry observers note that silverman, who runs Upcoming York nonprofit West Side Campaign Against Hunger, initially thought the driver wanted to use the bathroom at the church where the food distribution was taking place.
  • It has been revealed that "He was a full-time employee," Silverman said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

During the Covid-19 pandemic, Greg Silverman watched an MTA bus driver pull over on Manhattan's Upper West Side, let his passengers off and run across the street toward him.

Industry observers note that silverman, who runs Upcoming York nonprofit West Side Campaign Against Hunger, initially thought the driver wanted to use the bathroom at the church where the food distribution was taking place. Instead, the man asked, "Can I get some food?".

It has been revealed that "He was a full-time employee," Silverman said. "You are an essential personnel, making the city survive and you need food.".

In a recent development, now, Silverman said, his organization has seen demand surpass even the levels it observed during that time of crisis when the U.S. economy ground to a halt — and many of the people now seeking food also have jobs. Silverman expects the nonprofit to distribute as much as 6 million pounds of food this year.

"The height of the pandemic was not the height of need, by any means," he noted.

According to recent reports, the pressure on the emergency food system extends beyond Newly introduced York. Nationally, use of charitable food programs remains elevated as sustained inflation makes it harder for Americans to afford food, housing and healthcare. Higher prices come at the same time that the federal government has restricted food aid.

Sources indicate that the Department of Agriculture's latest annual report found that 13.7% of U.S. households, roughly 18.3 million households, experienced food insecurity in 2024. That rate was significantly higher than in every year from 2016 through 2021.

The pandemic initially brought a surge in demand for charitable food programs, which was followed by government support. In the years that followed, pandemic-era policies such as expanded Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, or SNAP, benefits, the enhanced child tax credit and school meal programs phased out as inflation spiked.

"This is not because you can't go to work," remarked City Harvest President Carlos Rodriguez. "Primarily, your work and your wages are just not keeping up with the way costs have gone up in the last five years alone.".

It has been revealed that city Harvest, which works with food providers across the five boroughs of Upcoming York, told CNBC 1 in 5 New Yorkers is right now experiencing food insecurity, or limited access to enough food because of a lack of money or other resources. That is up from 1 in 6 a year earlier, and 1 in 8 before the pandemic.

Average monthly visits to food pantries and soup kitchens in Fresh York are also 85% higher than before the pandemic, remarked Rodriguez.

In the Federal Reserve's October Beige Book, the central bank's Latest York regional branch described a sharp rise in first-time food pantry people. One nonprofit leader told the Federal Reserve Bank of New York that the strain was comparable to the pandemic, "but without the same philanthropic and government support.".

Data from Plentiful, a technology platform that connects people with food pantries and tracks their usage, also points to growing demand and limited resources.

"For pantries using our reservation and pre-registration features, we see that the overwhelming majority of those are at or over capacity," remarked Catherine Compitello, CEO of Plentiful. "Demand is growing while supply is not.".

Recent findings suggest that first-time users of Plentiful in New York City rose roughly 56% from August to October, Compitello remarked. It was the second-largest fall surge since 2016; the only larger one came during last year's federal government shutdown, when delayed SNAP benefits drove more people to seek food assistance.

Compitello said that when families have trouble affording essentials, they often prioritize healthcare, transportation, childcare and utilities, leaving food as the expense they cut back on.

Demand for food banks is rising in other regions of the country, and nonprofits are facing their own operational challenges as they try to meet it.

A spokesperson for the Los Angeles Regional Food Bank told CNBC the organization's diesel bill more than doubled in September, to roughly $75,000, adding to the cost of delivering food and running refrigerated trucks.

In a recent development, demand in the region is also spiking. Distribution in the Los Angeles area for January through September totaled 116 million pounds of food and grocery products — the equivalent of 93 million meals — and slightly higher than a near-record year in 2025, according to the Los Angeles Regional Food Bank.

Federal food aid changes have exacerbated the problems. Rodriguez of City Harvest described SNAP as a first line of defense against hunger, saying the program can provide as many as nine meals for every one meal the organization provides. But City Harvest has estimated at least 8.7% of SNAP recipients in Upcoming York City lost benefits over the past year, after congressional Republicans and President Donald Trump approved work certification requirements and changes to eligibility.

Recent findings suggest that the pressure is also mounting in Los Angeles County, where roughly 260,000 CalFresh recipients are subject to expanded federal work requirements that took effect in June. CalFresh is California's version of SNAP.

That does not mean all 260,000 will lose benefits, since people who meet the work requirements or qualify for an exemption can remain eligible. But a Los Angeles Regional Food Bank spokesperson told CNBC the changes add another layer of uncertainty for households already struggling with food costs.

In Atlanta, the pressure extends beyond the city itself to the surrounding region. The Atlanta Community Food Bank serves about 270,000 households a month, or nearly 700,000 people, through partner pantries across North Georgia. President and CEO Kyle Waide said the number of people it serves has jumped more than 70% in five years.

"Much of that increase is among people whose incomes are too high to qualify for federal benefit programs," remarked Waide.

Industry observers note that under current SNAP guidelines in Georgia, most households must have gross monthly income at or below 130% of the federal poverty level to qualify. They must also meet a separate net income test. For fiscal 2027, which began Oct. 1, the gross income limit is $2,960 a month for a household of three, or about $35,520 annually, and $3,575 a month for a household of four, or $42,900 a year.

More than 60% of Atlanta Community Food Bank clients have household incomes above the cutoff for SNAP eligibility, Waide said, generally in the mid-to-upper $30,000 range depending on household size. The food bank does not collect everyone's income, he said, but the figure is based on survey estimates.

Given those dynamics, Waide noted he does not expect the need to ease.

"We're preparing for the level of demand to stay where it is today, or even increase more," Waide stated. "We don't see a massive source of relief coming anytime soon.".
